#5257. Binance Shuts Down Transfers Involving MEXC and Its Affiliates

Just a few days after the U.S. Treasury took action to cut global crypto exchange MEXC off from the U.S. financial system, Binance has also announced strict regulatory actions against the exchange.

On Tuesday, November 10, Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by volume, announced its immediate decision to halt all transfers involving MEXC and all its affiliated companies.

Binance released an official announcement earlier today, warning users that it has stopped all trading services related to MEXC following new concerns about its legitimacy.

While the restrictions were announced to take effect immediately, Binance explained that its move follows the recent decision by the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) to designate MEXC as a Primary Money Laundering Concern.

As such, Binance has prohibited its users from directly or indirectly sending funds to, receiving funds from, or conducting transactions through Binance involving MEXC and its related entities.

The MEXC-affiliated entities mentioned by Binance include MEXC Global Limited, MEXC Estonia OÜ, MEXC Singapore Pte Ltd, MEXC Global Foundation Ltd, GIDA Technology AG, and several other companies and affiliates operating under the MEXC name.

Although MEXC is among the top 20 crypto exchanges in the world, FinCEN issued an order against MEXC on November 6, cutting the exchange off from the U.S. financial system amid recent fraud allegations.

Notably, the U.S. Treasury accused the exchange of facilitating at least $16 billion in illicit transactions tied to sanctions evasion and cybercrime and of defrauding people of their funds.

While Binance remains the first crypto exchange to take action in accordance with FinCEN’s rule, it appears that many other exchanges are lining up to take similar action.

#5253. Shiba Inu (SHIB) Scammers Fake 'Ryoshi' to Push 137 Scam Tokens and Dupe Investors

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. According to longtime SHIB community member Mazrael, since the SHIB deployer wallet went silent in October 2021, at least 137 scam tokens have falsely claimed that the SHIB deployer sent them the coins. The intent of scammers is to 'fake' Shiba Inu's pseudonymous founder, "Ryoshi," and the reason behind this is to appear legitimate: If "Ryoshi" sent it, people trust it.

Mazrael explains how this trick works: a token is just a program, and it keeps its own record of transfers. The scammer can write any address into that record as the sender. So these scammers write the SHIB deployer's address, and on Etherscan it looks like "Ryoshi" sent the token. However, the real SHIB deployer (0xB8f2…FA08) hasn't sent a single transaction since October 2021.

How scammers fake "Ryoshi" Since the SHIB deployer wallet went silent in October 2021, at least 137 scam tokens have pretended it sent them their coins. Why? To look legitimate. If "Ryoshi" sent it, people trust it. How the trick works: A token is just a program, and it keeps its own record of transfers. The scammer can write ANY address into that record as the sender. So they write the SHIB deployer's address, and on Etherscan it looks like "Ryoshi" sent you their token. But the deployer never signed anything. Click the transaction itself and look at "From". That's the wallet that really sent it, and it's never the SHIB deployer. The numbers: - 9,131+ fake transfers - 2,500+ wallets hit - 0 signed by the deployer Some of the fakes: APE, three "SHIBA INU2.0" tokens, ShibChain, SHIB DAO, METARUFFY, a token literally called "Ryoshi", Caw and Baby Caw, three fake "Shibarium" tokens (a year before the real one), "BONE2.0" and three "UNLEASHED DAO" tokens. Many got shilled by OGs and ex-admins as "Ryoshi-backed" to make them look legit. The real SHIB deployer (0xB8f2…FA08) hasn't sent a single transaction since October 2021. Always check who signed the transaction, not what the token says.

'The SHIB deployer never signed anything,' Mazrael stated, urging the crypto community to click on related token transactions and examine the "From" address, saying this is the wallet that sent it and was never the SHIB deployer.

Mazrael shared the numbers, outlining over 9,131 fake transfers, over 2,500 wallets hit, and zero signed by the SHIB deployer. He went on to name some of these fake tokens, adding that some of these tokens got promoted as "Ryoshi-backed" to make them look legitimate.

This disclosure warns crypto users to always check who signed the transaction, not what the token says.

In a separate post, Mazrael explained that nothing links the SHIB deployer address to any person.

The SHIB deployer (0xB8f2…FA08) only deployed one contract: SHIB, and it hasn't sent a single transaction since October 2021. It has no public signed message on record, either on-chain or on Etherscan.

LEASH, BONE, and TREAT each came from different deployers. Mazrael indicated that BONE's deployer is shiba-swap.eth, whereas LEASH came from '0xA221…1494,' the same key that deployed StarLink, whose own site names Woof Decentra as LEASH's developer. That key kept LEASH's rebase oracle, an admin key, for five years.

Cardano (ADA) hints at selling pressure below $0.18 as a large cluster of sell orders on major cryptocurrency exchanges is seen in CoinGlass data.

Order-book activity suggested a concentration of selling interest around the $0.177 to $0.179 area, which traders will be watching to see if ADA can break resistance.

CoinGlass reported a large sell wall of about $477,000 at $0.179 on Bitget's spot market. A large sell wall was also reported on the major crypto exchange Crypto.com, valued at around $415,000 near this price level on the spot market. Another large sell wall of about $445,400 at $0.177 was reported on Binance's futures market.

If sellers hold their ground, these concentrated orders could be a hurdle for Cardano to climb above $0.18, as it is currently trading at $0.176, down 1.59% over the past 24 hours. A sell wall is a big cluster of limit sell orders at a price level that can soak up buying pressure as the market approaches that price.

But just because there are large sell orders does not mean the price will be rejected. If there is enough demand to buy, it might soak up the supply.

The region $0.177-$0.179 is an important area to watch now. How much of the reported sell orders Cardano can absorb will be key in deciding whether buyers can recover momentum or sellers will remain in control below $0.18.

Cardano’s open interest (OI)—the total value or number of derivatives contracts that have not been settled—has gone up over the past 24 hours, a sign of rising trader participation and new positioning in the ADA derivatives market.

According to CoinGlass, Cardano's open interest was up 5.42% over the past day to $395.09 million

While on-chain data highlights potential sell walls for Cardano, large buy walls coincidentally reside slightly below where the ADA price currently trades. Cardano's buying interest could pick up in the range between $0.17 and $0.175, as clusters of buy walls are located at those levels. CoinGlass reports spot net taker selling of $1.27 million for Cardano. In addition, futures taker buys exceeded sells by 3.9%, suggesting buyers are relatively in control.

#5246. Why Is Crypto Crashing Today? Bitcoin Falls Below $73K as Zcash (ZEC) Leads Crypto Losses

Why is crypto crashing? A hot CPI report raised Fed hike bets. ZEC fell below $1,000, the worst of 20 large coins this week.

Why is crypto crashing on Wednesday, November 11? The sell-off that began with Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report has carried into today, and almost every major coin is lower.

Bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $73,000 on Tuesday, touching $72,727 on Binance, and now trades at about $73,800. Ether (ETH) briefly slipped to $2,006, while XRP and Solana (SOL) are down 2% to 3% in 24 hours. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a daily gauge of market mood from 0 to 100, has fallen to 29.

The report changed what traders expect from the Federal Reserve. Bond yields jumped, and bets on a larger December rate hike nearly tripled within two hours.

One coin is falling much harder than the rest. Zcash (ZEC) is a cryptocurrency launched in 2016 that lets users hide the sender, the receiver and the amount of a payment. It dropped below $1,000 on Wednesday for the first time since September 5. ZEC now trades at about $966, down 15.4% in 24 hours and 24.8% in a week.

ZEC has been one of this year’s best performers. It rose from about $526 on January 1 to a closing high of $1,653 on September 26. We checked the 20 largest coins on Binance, and ZEC fell the most over both the day and the week, even though it is still up 89% in 2026.

Trader 0x8742 opened a 10x long on 18,000 $ZEC ($17.63M) and is now down over $2.8M.

Liquidation price: $895.46.https://t.co/azzt3xvmay pic.twitter.com/wczndt7doC

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 11, 2026

So why are the markets spooked, and why is ZEC taking the hardest hit?

Inflation came in hot. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast.

That reading crossed a line the Fed had drawn. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech hours before the report that core inflation of about 0.3% would make a half-point hike in December worth considering.

Traders took him at his word. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 0.5 percentage point or more in December went from 4.4% just before the report to 12.8% two hours later. They sit at 9.4% now, while a standard quarter-point hike is priced at 85.5%.

Higher rates hurt crypto in a simple way. They make cash and bonds pay more, so money flows out of riskier bets. On Tuesday, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose from 4.86% to 4.98%.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

ZEC had the most to give back. We compared the price changes of 20 large coins on Binance over the past week and since January 1.

When markets get nervous, traders tend to sell what has made them the most money. ZEC has fallen 41% from its September 26 closing high of $1,653.

Borrowed money made the drop faster. On Hyperliquid, ZEC fell from $1,199.20 to $965.79 in less than a day. Lookonchain counted 32 traders holding more than $1 million each in leveraged bets on a rising ZEC price. Of those, 27 are now losing money, with about $23.7 million in paper losses between them.

Sharp drops have not always lasted. Since January 2025, ZEC has fallen 12% or more in a single day 14 times on Binance. Seven days later, it was higher eight times, with a median gain of 6.5%.

EXPLORE: Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

ZEC trades at about $966. It touched $961.07 on Wednesday, its lowest price since September 4.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, ZEC has fallen below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1,200.68. It is still above its 200-day EMA at $872.23.

For Bitcoin, the line to watch is Tuesday’s low of $72,727. Below that, $68,902, the August 20 low, is the next support.

So, why is crypto crashing? A hot inflation report raised the odds of a bigger Fed hike, and ZEC’s leveraged bulls are paying the most for it. A daily close back above $1,050 would be the first sign the selling is easing.

Supply has continued to shift into newer hands, as the short-term-to-long-term holder supply ratio and the share of hot capital remain elevated. Short-term holders now sit near break-even, and realized losses clearly outweigh profits.

#5238. Don’t Store Crypto on iPhone, Ledger CTO Says

Ledger Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet has recently warned cryptocurrency holders not to store critical wallet information on their iPhones, as the security threat is on the rise.

In his recent post on X, the Ledger executive highlighted the fact that vulnerabilities that can leak important data are now becoming more and more accessible for hackers to exploit.

"Unfortunately this kind of vulnerability used to be very expensive and reserved to high potential attackers," Guillemet tweeted.

However, he pointed out that we're now on the verge of seeing the costs of such vulnerabilities go down to zero, meaning that it could become very easy for cybercriminals to exploit them on a massive scale.

"Simply don't store any valuable in your mobile. Especially not your crypto seeds," the Ledger CTO cautioned.

His words came in response to an urgent security alert published by crypto exchange Binance over a vulnerability that was found in Apple's iOS operating system.

In particular, cryptocurrency exchange Binance reported a vulnerability, dubbed worse_query, which can allow malicious applications to gain access to files of other applications installed on the same device.

As specified by the exchange, this security flaw affects iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1 and 27.2.

This means that crypto wallet recovery phrases, private keys and login credentials can be at risk, as they may be stored in accessible local files.

Binance underscored that this concern isn't exclusive to the exchange's app alone, while adding that the vulnerability can have an impact on the entire crypto space.

The exchange recommended that users uninstall apps that were downloaded from untrusted sources, update their operating systems and avoid installing any unauthorized software.

Binance also advised users to transfer their funds to newly created wallets on clean devices if they think their wallets may have been compromised.

Apple published new security updates on Nov. 9. However, it's not clear if they are enough to fully patch this vulnerability. Still, there have been no confirmed crypto thefts specifically linked to the exploit.

Guillemet's warning comes a month after Ledger's major security incident involving compromised hardware wallets.

Back in October, French cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker Ledger admitted that some hardware wallets distributed by its Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis had been tampered with.

It turned out that hackers managed to install complex hardware implants in legitimate Ledger devices. With that, hackers were able to intercept users' recovery phrases when people were setting up their Ledger wallets for the first time.

As shown by Ledger's investigation, malicious implants were capable of capturing the 24-word recovery phrase that appears on the Ledger device screen and then passing it to attackers via a cellular connection.

Blockchain sleuths estimated that this incident might have led to more than $86 million in crypto losses. However, Ledger itself didn't confirm the total amount.

#5237. Bank of America Warns of 50 bps Fed Hike in December: Is Bitcoin Heading for Another 2022-Style Drop?

Bank of America (BofA) says hot CPI puts a 50bps December Fed hike on the table. BTC fell a week later after 5 of the last 6 big hikes.

Bank of America said this week that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates by half a percentage point in December. The warning came after Tuesday’s October inflation report ran hotter than expected for a third month in a row. In Bitcoin news, the coin trades at $73,888 on Binance, down 0.6% in 24 hours. It dropped to $72,727 on Tuesday after the report, its lowest price since August 20.

The bank still expects the Fed to raise rates by 0.25 percentage points, or 25 basis points (bps), at its December 8–9 meeting. But it says the case for a bigger move is growing, and it calls the Fed’s decision to hold rates in October a possible policy mistake.

Traders are starting to listen. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 50 bps or more in December rose from 0.6% on Monday to 11.4% on Wednesday.

BANK OF AMERICA WARNS FED COULD DELIVER 50BPS HIKE IN DECEMBER

Bank of America says October's hot CPI report virtually guarantees a December Fed rate hike — and opens the door to a larger 50bps move.

Headline CPI rose 0.4%, while core CPI climbed 0.3%, marking a third…

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 11, 2026

The bank’s call rests on three months of hot data. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. Both beat forecasts, the third upside surprise in a row in the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.

Bank of America now estimates that core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred measure, is running at 3.3% a year. The Fed’s target is 2%. The bank says price rises are spreading from goods to services, with electronics, airfares and hotels leading the increases.

Its base case is still a 25 bps hike in December. The change is in the risks: a 50 bps move is now possible, and the bank sees a growing chance of another hike in January instead of March.

The bank is not alone. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech on Tuesday morning that he leans toward a 25 bps hike in December. If core inflation came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 50 bps hike “should be considered.” It did.

Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more. That tends to pull money out of risky assets like BTC, and a faster pace of hikes pulls harder.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

The size of the hike has mattered for BTC. We measured Bitcoin’s price on Binance from the 2 p.m. ET announcement of each Fed rate hike since 2022 to one week later. That covers 12 hikes: six of 50 bps or more and six of 25 bps.

After the six big hikes, BTC was lower a week later five times. The median move was a 6% drop. The worst came after the 50 bps hike in May 2022, when BTC fell 23% in a week.

After the six 25 bps hikes, the picture was milder. BTC was lower a week later four times, but the median move was a drop of just 0.6%.

The record comes with a caveat. All six big hikes happened in 2022, a bear market that also saw the collapses of Terra in May and FTX in November. Those crashes made the falls after the May and November hikes worse.

The most recent hike was a 25 bps move on September 16. BTC rose 11.3% in the week after it, as the uncertainty that had built up before the meeting cleared. That makes the size of December’s hike, more than the hike itself, the Bitcoin news to watch.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin CPI Reaction: 10 of 13 Cool Inflation Reports Triggered an Hourly Gain – Can Inflation Data Reverse the Downtrend?

BTC trades at $73,888, down 0.6% in 24 hours and 5.8% over the past week. It sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight, on the daily chart. The 50-day EMA stands at $78,897 and the 200-day EMA at $76,449.

For Bitcoin news, the next test is the Fed’s own message. Traders already expect a 25 bps hike. If more officials join Waller and Bank of America in backing 50 bps, BTC may have to defend $72,727 before the December 9 decision.

However, he believes the community has placed too much emphasis on Ripple, creating a misleading perception that XRP’s value and long-term prospects depend on a single corporate player.

“XRP’s value and narrative should never have been perceived as being based solely on the actions of one player,” Philion stated.

The Flare co-founder stressed that XRP has always had greater potential beyond Ripple’s activities, which partly motivated Flare’s creation. In his view, expanding the range of applications available to XRP holders is essential to strengthening the token’s utility, market narrative, and long-term value proposition.

Philion challenged the XRP community to shift its attention toward three fundamental questions: what holders are doing to put their XRP to work, how they can demonstrate its value to people who have yet to invest, and what steps they are taking to transform the cryptocurrency from a speculative holding into usable capital.

He suggested that answering these questions requires more than simply waiting for Ripple to announce new partnerships, products, or adoption initiatives. Instead, XRP holders and developers must actively contribute to building financial applications and use cases that give the asset greater utility.

Philion specifically pointed to Flare as a way to achieve this goal, arguing that the network offers an opportunity to expand what holders can do with their XRP and help separate the asset’s value proposition from Ripple’s corporate decisions.

The Flare co-founder’s remarks come amid growing frustration among XRP holders over the cryptocurrency’s weak price performance. XRP has shed approximately 51% of its value over the past year, trading at around $1.10 at the time of the report. The prolonged decline has also reignited questions about what could drive the token’s next recovery and whether its prospects are too closely tied to Ripple’s business activities.

The criticism has also extended to Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz, who recently faced questions about XRP’s disappointing performance. Schwartz pushed back against suggestions that he could influence the token’s market value, explaining that his ability to move XRP’s price was extremely limited.

Separately, technical analyst Dark Defender remains confident in his double-digit XRP prediction in a recent X post, insisting that the token’s recent decline has not invalidated his broader technical setup.

“Nothing has changed in the structure,” the analyst opined, pointing to the $1.21 and $1.12 support levels he had identified in his October 25 analysis.

According to Dark Defender, XRP’s latest pullback remains within the price scenario he had already mapped out. Rather than abandoning his bullish outlook, he maintained that the cryptocurrency’s movement toward these support zones does not necessarily signal a breakdown of the structure underpinning his longer-term $10 target.

Dark Defender’s earlier Elliott Wave chart outlined a potential rally toward the $10.1101 region. However, reaching that level would require a dramatic recovery from current prices. At $1.10, XRP would need to surge about 809% to reach $10, while climbing to $10.1101 would require roughly an 819% advance.

Given roughly 63.52 billion XRP in circulation, a $10 valuation would put the cryptocurrency’s market capitalization at around $635.2 billion. Reaching the higher $10.1101 target would push its implied market value to around $642.2 billion.

The Bitwise XRP ETF, listed under the ticker XRP, was introduced in November 2025.

The ETF enables traditional investors to invest in the Ripple-linked cryptocurrency without needing to buy and hold XRP tokens themselves.

Although Rothschild Investment has invested in the XRP ETF, it is not a significant part of its overall portfolio.

The firm’s total portfolio value for 13F-reportable holdings is around $2.69 billion.

Rothschild Investment holds much larger stakes in Bitcoin and Ethereum investments.

When it comes to cryptocurrencies, Rothschild Investment’s largest holding is in the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF by BlackRock, where the company owns 40,188 shares worth around $1.9 million.

Additionally, Rothschild Investment reported holding $911,300 in the Grayscale Bitcoin Trust ETF and $335,160 in the Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust ETF.

Other Bitcoin-related investments include the Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust ETF ($125,113), VanEck Bitcoin ETF ($118,100), Bitwise Bitcoin ETF ($116,802) and Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund ($2,107).

In total, the seven Bitcoin investments represent around $3.51 million in reported holdings.

Rothschild Investment also has stakes in the Grayscale Ethereum Staking ETF worth $538,622 and the Bitwise Ethereum ETF worth $476,500.

The company also has a significant holding in the Bitwise Crypto Industry Innovators ETF, with 24,250 shares worth $615,223.

The firm owns $38,360 worth of shares in the Grayscale CoinDesk Crypto 5 ETF.

Finally, it has invested $69,900 in a Solana ETF.

Aside from cryptocurrency investment funds, Rothschild Investment has shares in publicly traded companies that are heavily involved in the digital asset space.

Michael Saylor’s Strategy is one such holding, with a $530,763 investment.

Other holdings include Coinbase Global ($86,681), Block ($125,060) and Riot Platforms ($42,980), a Bitcoin mining company.

#5226. NEAR AI Discloses SGLang Security Incident and Revokes Exposed API Keys

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: NEAR AI has published a security incident report involving an SGLang vulnerability in legacy deployments. The company says it revoked exposed credentials and addressed the issue, while acknowledging that some requests could have been observed. Its findings distinguish confirmed exposure from data it has no evidence was accessed.

A security disclosure from NEAR AI highlights a familiar danger in the expanding AI-agent industry: sophisticated applications can inherit serious problems from the infrastructure they run on.

In a November 9 incident report, the organization described an SGLang remote-code-execution vulnerability affecting legacy deployment infrastructure. The investigation identified roughly 100 user details and 18 agents in the affected context, with two Cloud API keys exposed and subsequently revoked.

The company said there was no evidence that stored Private Chat content had been compromised. It also cautioned that some requests made on November 8 could potentially have been observed. Those are not contradictory statements: investigators may find no evidence of one category of access while being unable to rule out another.

AI applications are assembled from multiple components: model servers, request routers, authentication systems, logging and the user-facing product. SGLang is part of the infrastructure used to serve language models. A flaw at that level can create opportunities for attackers before a user ever interacts with an onchain wallet or signs a transaction.

Remote-code-execution issues can be particularly serious because they may allow an attacker to run unauthorized instructions in the affected environment. The scope of what follows depends on the privileges, network access and data available to that environment.

For readers, this means the incident should not be conflated with a vulnerability in the NEAR blockchain consensus rules or a general compromise of all NEAR wallets. The report concerns particular AI-serving infrastructure and its potential exposures.

According to the published account, the team investigated affected deployments, revoked the two exposed API keys, remediated the vulnerability and notified impacted parties. Those are necessary containment steps, though the effectiveness of remediation depends on whether other pathways remain open and whether credentials are rotated wherever they were used.

The report’s numerical counts also need careful interpretation. Approximately 100 user details and 18 agents do not mean 100 users lost funds or that every associated request was read. Exposure, confirmed access and financial loss are separate findings that should not be collapsed into one sensational claim.

Crypto firms are integrating AI into development, support, trading and operational workflows. An AI tool may eventually handle private business information even when it cannot directly sign onchain transactions. That raises the value of conventional safeguards: isolating services, limiting credentials, monitoring access and maintaining incident-response plans.

The broader institutional push toward blockchain infrastructure, including the NYSE’s tokenized-securities plans, depends on more than smart-contract security. Offchain services must also be robust. A well-audited ledger cannot compensate for a compromised application server.

Likewise, rising institutional attention to crypto assets, which NewsBTC tracks through developments such as Ether ETF flows, makes operational controls increasingly consequential. These links are contextual rather than a claim that those products were involved in this incident.

Affected users should rely on NEAR AI’s direct notifications and published guidance. Where they have used credentials in related services, reviewing access permissions and rotating keys is prudent. Users should not assume that ordinary NEAR wallet keys have been exposed simply because the company reported an infrastructure flaw.

The most important follow-up is a clear technical postmortem explaining affected versions, root cause and validation of the fixes. For companies building AI agents around finance, the episode is a reminder that infrastructure security and candid disclosure are both part of earning trust.

#5225. Bitcoin Price Slides Toward $73K as Nvidia Plunges 9% and MSCI Drops Saylor’s Strategy

BTC slips as Nvidia sinks 9% after hours and MSCI drops Strategy. ETFs lost $1.88B in November, 94% of it from IBIT.

In Bitcoin news, the coin fell from $74,811 to $73,480 within two hours of the U.S. close. Bitcoin slipped overnight after two shocks hit U.S. markets after Wednesday’s close. Nvidia shares fell about 9% in after-hours trading on a new report about CEO Jensen Huang. Index provider MSCI also confirmed it will remove Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, from its global indexes.

It trades at $73,588 on Binance on Thursday morning, down 0.4% in 24 hours and 5.8% in a week.

The funds are not helping. U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) lost $299.8 million on Wednesday, their fifth straight day of outflows. Nasdaq futures are down 0.9%.

Bitcoin ETFs Shed $300 Million, Ether Funds Lose $145 Million

According to SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $300 million in net outflows on November 11, while Morgan Stanley's MSBT led individual fund inflows with $8.96 million. Spot Ethereum ETFs saw $145 million in… pic.twitter.com/5sn88B2JQX

— Wu Blockchain (@WuBlockchain) November 12, 2026

So what happened, and how much of the selling comes from the ETFs?

The first hit came from Nvidia, the world’s most valuable chipmaker. The New York Times reported on Wednesday evening that Huang had a second relationship with a senior employee who reports to him. The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to remove him as CEO.

Nvidia had closed the day up 2.9% at $173.73. Within two hours, it traded at $157.99, down 9.1%. It is still down 8.6% before Thursday’s open. Nvidia has lost about 15% since last Friday. It first fell on Monday, after its board opened a separate probe into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Bitcoin has traded closely with tech stocks this year, and it fell with them. Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 1.1% in the same two hours.

The second hit is closer to crypto. MSCI, whose indexes guide trillions of dollars in index funds, will delete Strategy from its global indexes after the market close on November 30. It ruled that Strategy looks more like an investment fund holding Bitcoin than an operating business. Japan’s Metaplanet and Upexi are also being removed.

Funds that track those indexes will have to sell their Strategy shares. JPMorgan earlier estimated that selling at about $2.8 billion. Strategy says the funds hold about 13 million shares, 3.1% of its stock. Its shares are down 1.8% before the open.

#5222. BitGo Posts $44M Quarterly Profit as Platform Assets Grow, But Adjusted EBITDA Stays Negative

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: BitGo reported roughly $44.1 million in third-quarter net income even as adjusted EBITDA remained negative at about $4.3 million. Assets on its platform rose to $59.9 billion on the company’s normalized measure. The headline revenue figure includes substantial direct costs, so it should not be treated like a conventional software sales number.

BitGo’s third-quarter results offer a useful case study in why crypto-company earnings need more than a glance at the revenue line. The custody and infrastructure provider reported a positive net result, growing platform assets and continued expansion of its customer base. Yet one measure of ongoing profitability remained below zero.

In its earnings exhibit filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, the company reported net income of roughly $44.1 million and adjusted EBITDA of negative $4.3 million for the third quarter of 2026. Those two figures tell different stories because they do not include the same items.

Reported total revenue was approximately $2.85 billion, compared with around $5.81 billion in the comparable year-earlier quarter. At first glance that looks like an extraordinary contraction for a custody business. But BitGo also reported about $2.81 billion in direct costs against the latest revenue total.

The large figures reflect the accounting presentation of transaction-related activity, rather than pure software or recurring subscription income. The spread between revenue and direct costs is therefore an important part of understanding the economics. Comparing headline gross revenue with that of a conventional enterprise-software company could mislead readers.

The company attributed positive GAAP net income in part to treasury-related appreciation, while its adjusted EBITDA measure was still negative. Investors should examine those adjustments rather than assuming accounting profit automatically equals positive cash generation from ordinary operations.

BitGo said normalized assets on platform rose 31.9% to $59.9 billion and normalized staked assets grew 41.1%. It also cited approximately 6,640 clients. Those metrics provide a view into demand for its services even as fluctuations in transaction-related revenue complicate the income statement.

The distinction matters to institutions selecting custodians. A provider’s commercial footprint can expand while costs, pricing or exceptional items cause a temporary mismatch between headline earnings and adjusted operating profit. Conversely, assets under service are not the same as assets BitGo owns or can freely use.

NewsBTC recently described BitGo’s role in custody arrangements for a Grayscale-related Hyperliquid product. We also covered plans for BitGo to provide access to a WisdomTree tokenized Treasury product. Both illustrate why custody businesses compete on institutional integrations as well as transactional volume.

The figures reinforce the idea that crypto infrastructure companies are not interchangeable with the tokens they support. A higher Bitcoin price may lift the value of assets in custody, while trading patterns, service mix, expenses and treasury changes can pull reported results in different directions.

Normalized platform assets also depend on the company’s definition of that measure, which readers should consult in the filing. It is not identical to customer deposits at a bank and should not be used as a proxy for BitGo’s own balance-sheet cash.

The useful follow-ups will be whether client and staking activity translate into better margins, how much of future earnings comes from recurring custody services, and whether adjusted operating profitability improves. Any forward-looking forecast should be separated from the quarter’s actual results.

BitGo has shown growth in assets handled and a positive bottom-line accounting result. But the negative adjusted EBITDA means the operating-quality story is still more complicated than a single profit headline might suggest.

#5219. HIVE Reports $84.9M Revenue as AI GPU Business Grows 71% Amid Mining Pressures

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: HIVE Digital reported $84.9 million in fiscal second-quarter revenue and roughly 71% growth in its AI-focused BUZZ GPU business. The company also recorded a substantial quarterly loss, including a mining-equipment impairment. The results show both the promise and cost of shifting computing capacity toward AI services.

Bitcoin miners have spent much of 2026 trying to turn their access to electricity, land and data centers into businesses that can serve more than one market. HIVE Digital’s latest numbers put a price tag on that strategy.

The company said its fiscal second quarter, ended September 30, 2026, brought in approximately $84.9 million of revenue. Its BUZZ high-performance-computing division generated about $8.8 million, an increase of 70.7% from the comparable period. HIVE also reported about $139 million in cash on the balance sheet.

The growth is meaningful, but the AI arm remains far smaller than the company’s combined operations. A rapidly growing new division does not automatically replace the economics of Bitcoin mining.

HIVE reported a quarterly net loss in the region of $78 million and included a mining-equipment impairment of approximately $31.2 million. Impairments are generally noncash accounting charges in the period they are recorded, but they can still indicate that expected future economic value has fallen.

That distinction is important. A loss containing a major impairment is not the same as the business spending an identical amount of cash in the quarter. Equally, treating impairments as irrelevant would miss what they say about the pressure on older machines or assumptions about their earning potential.

Mining hardware has a useful life shaped by electricity prices, network difficulty, equipment efficiency and Bitcoin’s market value. When those assumptions change, a fleet that looked attractive two years ago may not justify its former carrying value.

The case for AI data centers is that demand for specialized computing may offer a revenue stream less closely tied to Bitcoin’s mining difficulty. But supplying GPU services requires capital, customer relationships, network infrastructure and operational expertise different from the work of running application-specific mining rigs.

NewsBTC has tracked miners making that transition, including Riot’s Bitcoin sales alongside its AI-data-center ambitions. HIVE’s BUZZ expansion is another version of the same strategic question: how quickly can an established miner earn durable income from compute services?

Partnerships and infrastructure projects are relevant here too. Our reporting on TeraWulf’s growth in AI leasing shows how the business of securing power-intensive sites and monetizing them through leases has become competitive. Possessing a data center does not guarantee demand for the GPUs housed in it.

Future reports should clarify how much revenue the AI division earns, whether its margins justify continued capital investment and how the mining segment performs as difficulty changes. Total company revenue can rise or fall for reasons unrelated to the profitability of the new computing business.

Investors should also watch the company’s liquidity, debt commitments and equipment spending. The $139 million cash figure is helpful context, but not a substitute for understanding cash consumption and future construction obligations.

HIVE is presenting itself as a dual-engine business. The latest quarter demonstrates that GPU services are growing quickly, while the bottom-line loss shows why the transition remains a work in progress rather than an accomplished turnaround.

#5217. End of Crypto Hardware Wallets? Sui Cancels Suiball Wallet Amid Cybersecurity Risks

The hardware wallets industry is taking a huge hit in 2026, and Ledger's supply chain exploit set a certain fact in stone: no wallet is secure, no algorithm is uncrackable. As a reminder: back in October, Ledger confirmed the placement of an unauthorized electronic plate inside of their device sold via reseller CryptoBills.

Units sold in Southeast Asia had an exploit which allowed illicit actors to steal recovery phrases during the setup of the wallet.

Most likely outcome for the cybersecurity industry would be AI protecting itself from AI-based reverse-engineering. This is not taking into consideration things like one happened with Ledger.

Sui Hardware wallet is no different: they understand the risks and take them seriously on such extent where they simply decide not to ship it, avoiding unnecessary risks. Suiball, a hardware wallet built natively for Sui, announced its closure on November 11, after the Sui Foundation decided that backing a hardware wallet project is too risky after the recent attacks across the industry.

Surprisingly, the first batch of wallets have already been developed, manufactured and ready to be sent out to the first owners. However, the Sui Foundation decided to play it safe and avoid potential issues with those who might want to reverse-engineer the wallet or plant a backdoor somewhere along the supply chain.

The recent Fable 5.2 release suggests an advanced level of work with electronics, hardware devices and firmwares, which is the exact field hackers might need to attack hardware wallets using AI. Anthropic states that Fable 5.2, released on November 9, designed three working devices from one-paragraph prompts.

Those devices went through the whole cycle with its partner Diode, including schematics, circuit boards and firmware. Luckily, there's no proven link between the Fable 5.2 release and Suiball's closure, as the project hasn't mentioned AI at all.

Most of the hardware wallets pre-orders were on-chain, so users will simply receive their USDC back.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Liquidity in the stablecoin space has contracted rapidly, reducing one of the most significant sources of buying power from crypto markets. Over the last 60 days ending on the 7th of November, according to CryptoQuant, Tether [USDT] saw its market capitalization drop by $6.6 billion.

This represents the largest such contraction since CryptoQuant began tracking this metric in 2022, exceeding a $3.2 billion decline in the wake of the FTX collapse. Trends suggest that investors are withdrawing capital from stablecoins instead of holding them ready for use in crypto trades.

Overall, stablecoin capitalization now stands at approximately $290 billion. With less capital available to provide dollar backing for potential sales and new position entries, there appears to be fewer dollars remaining to fund a crypto market recovery.

At the same time, a decrease in demand of approximately 284,000 BTC over thirty days is evident for Bitcoin [BTC]. As such, if no additional capital flows into stablecoins, then buyers may experience difficulty in sustaining a rally.

As stablecoin capitalization declines, large financial institutions have positioned themselves to capture a greater percentage of the overall market. Project Faro, a joint stablecoin venture, has obtained $270 million from 21 major financial firms.

This includes Goldman Sachs, Citi, Santander, and Deutsche Bank to fund operations over five years prior to launching their dollar-backed stablecoin during the first half of 2027. Still, a euro back stablecoin is expected to follow.

This funding illustrates increasing interest among large established banks regarding participation in the stablecoin market. This is as the overall capitalization of the stablecoin space dropped to $290 billion.

Yet entering the market will be easier than displacing existing leaders. Tether and Circle control roughly 85% of supply, making adoption and liquidity key challenges.

Although Project Faro is preparing for launch, the true measure of success will depend upon how businesses utilize the payment features provided by the project.

As Project Faro aims to facilitate cross-border transactions using dollar-backed stablecoins, they could potentially eliminate reliance on slower bank processing times associated with cross-border transactions.

Companies would be able to send dollar-backed tokens across borders without being required to wait for the standard settlement period. Payment speed and access to funds may also be improved for multinational corporations that operate in various markets.

However, recurrent business payment will ultimately define whether Project Faro achieves its ultimate goal of establishing a meaningful role for its stablecoin products and services as a result of its banking ambitions.

#5214. Binance Warns of Apple iOS Flaw That Could Expose iPhone Users' Private Keys

Binance Warns of Apple iOS Flaw That Could Expose iPhone Users' Private Keys

Binance has warned iPhone users about a vulnerability in Apple's iOS that it says could let malicious apps read files stored by other apps, putting crypto wallet seed phrases, private keys and login credentials at risk.

The flaw, dubbed "worse_query," affects iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1 and 27.2, the exchange tweeted on Tuesday. "This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance," it said.

A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem. This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.…

Binance urged users to delete any apps installed from untrusted sources, such as sideloaded or manually signed app files, and to update iOS and all apps to the latest official versions. Anyone who suspects a breach should move their funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions, it said.

iPhone apps normally run inside a sandbox, which stops them from accessing other apps' private files. A researcher who goes by forcequitOS published worse_query on GitHub as a sandbox escape for iOS 26.0 through 26.7.2 and iOS 27.2, describing it as a proof of concept for developers that "isn't useful by itself." Among the locations it can reach is the folder where iOS apps store their data, according to the repository, which calls it the "direct successor" to an earlier exploit, bad_query. There have been no confirmed reports of crypto being stolen using the flaw.

Apple released iOS 27.2.1 on Monday, a day after the proof of concept was published. Its security notes list fixes for nine vulnerabilities, including an authorization issue in App Intents through which "an app may be able to access sensitive user data," as well as several Bluetooth and iMessage flaws.

However, the notes do not mention worse_query or its researcher, and Apple has not publicly confirmed whether the update addresses the flaw Binance described. At least one security expert believes it does. 23pds, chief information security officer at blockchain security firm SlowMist, urged users to update to iOS 27.2.1, saying in a tweet that the update would block the worse_query sandbox escape, along with other threats.

It is not the first time attackers have targeted Apple devices. Earlier this year, Google warned of iOS malware that targeted crypto apps on unpatched devices, while in August, the Dutch national cyber agency said hackers were exploiting a flaw in Apple's macOS Screen Sharing feature to plant Monero miners on Macs.

#5213. Deutsche Bank Opens Digital Asset Custody to Paying Institutional Clients

Deutsche Bank opens up digital asset custody to paying institutional clients. The service includes storage, user experience improvements, and accessibility via the bank's own gateways. The bank announced the launch on November 11, as DB's official website reveals.

This is an improvement in the field of institutional adoption, even though it comes at a time when it might be unwarranted. The market is experiencing serious issues and constant outflows from both retail and institutional investors.

Surprisingly, the bank can provide both warm and cold storage options available directly through DB's infrastructure. According to the landing page, the platform will provide key storage via Hardware Security Modules. Access goes through Autobahn, the bank's own multi-channel gateway.

Compliance will also be handled by Deutsche Bank. Initially, the service will focus on core functions: custody of digital assets and transfers, with further capabilities planned.

The Asian market has yet to receive similar treatment. For now, the service is available in the EU, operating out of DB AG Frankfurt. An expansion to Asia is reportedly planned for 2027, though the details are yet to be confirmed.

Additionally, DB announced support for euro stablecoins such as EURC and EURAU, in addition to BTC, ETH, and USDC. This is an attempt to promote the adoption of EU-issued stablecoins as part of a strategy aimed at moving away from USDT dominance. EURAU is issued by AllUnity, a joint venture that includes DWS, the asset manager majority-owned by Deutsche Bank.

Self-custody or banks: that is the real question here. Industry experts such as Bloomberg's ETF analyst Eric Balchunas suggest that self-custody has been a worse option and that a custodian with funds protection and insurance is a better option for regular investors. Even Binance founder CZ admitted after the Ledger incident that self-custody comes with extra responsibilities.

Back in August, a Coldcard exploit drained 1,816 BTC from more than 5,000 cold-storage addresses, according to Fortune.

However, it puts some pressure on those who might receive their funds from grey sources. Unfortunately for them, a bank custodian creates another barrier, as every deposit has to go through the bank's compliance checks.

#5212. Bitdeer Revenue Jumps 89% to $320.7M as AI Backlog Grows Despite Quarterly Loss

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Bitdeer posted record third-quarter revenue of $320.7 million, up 89% year over year, while reporting a $125.5 million net loss. Its stated AI-cloud backlog approached $2.9 billion, highlighting demand potential but not revenue already earned or cash already collected.

Bitdeer has delivered one of the clearest examples yet of a Bitcoin mining business trying to transform itself into a provider of broader computing infrastructure. Its latest quarter brought record revenue and a sizable artificial-intelligence cloud order pipeline. It also remained deeply unprofitable under standard accounting measures.

In its November 10 third-quarter results announcement, the company reported $320.7 million in revenue, an 89% increase from the year-earlier period. Adjusted EBITDA rose to about $69.6 million, while the GAAP net loss reached approximately $125.5 million.

Those measures differ, and the gap requires careful reading. Management highlighted changes in the fair value of digital-asset-related borrowing, including a $54.6 million noncash item, as one factor in the accounting result.

The figure likely to attract the most attention is Bitdeer’s reported AI-cloud backlog of approximately $2.9 billion. A backlog represents contracted or expected future services under the company’s reporting definitions, rather than cash already received or recognized quarterly revenue.

The amount eventually converted into sales will depend on contract delivery, customer demand, capacity coming online and the terms attached to commitments. Investors should seek disclosures about timing and any conditions that could delay or reduce the total.

Nevertheless, a substantial backlog can signal customer interest for specialized infrastructure. That is particularly valuable in a business where constructing or equipping data centers involves significant upfront spending.

Bitdeer reported production of 3,855 Bitcoin during the quarter and said it held 47 Bitcoin at quarter-end. Those figures help distinguish operating output from Bitcoin retained on the balance sheet. Production can be high even if a firm sells most of the coins to fund operations, equipment or other projects.

The company also reported approximately $213.7 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash. A cash balance should be considered alongside capital commitments, financing costs and planned expansion rather than treated as unencumbered profits from AI.

NewsBTC has reported on Riot’s decision to sell Bitcoin as it pursues major AI infrastructure contracts. The miners are pursuing different projects, but both illustrate a sector balancing near-term funding needs with investments that may generate future revenue.

Our coverage of Soluna and Bitdeer’s Texas infrastructure agreement adds a concrete example of why access to powered sites and commercial partnerships remains important as the competition for computing capacity grows.

Adjusted EBITDA may help investors evaluate operating performance before certain expenses and valuation changes. It is not identical to net income or free cash flow. A company can report a positive adjusted measure and still incur losses, financing costs and heavy investment requirements.

That is why the $125.5 million net loss deserves to stand alongside the $320.7 million revenue headline. Both are true, and neither alone gives a complete picture.

Bitdeer’s next reporting periods need to show when AI-cloud backlog turns into delivered services, how those services contribute to margins and how much capital they consume. Improvements in mining efficiency and power costs will also remain relevant.

The latest results point to striking revenue momentum and a potentially meaningful new business line. They do not yet demonstrate that the shift toward AI has resolved the financial volatility historically associated with Bitcoin mining.

#5209. Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

The crypto market crash deepens as $1B+ in longs get liquidated. Bitcoin sits mid-range at $72,969; fear at 28 isn’t a bottom yet.

Bitcoin fell below $73,000 on Thursday, November 12, extending a week-long crypto market crash in which traders who bet on a rebound were forced out of their positions again and again.

Bitcoin touched $72,735 on Binance, a hair above Tuesday’s $72,727 low and its weakest price since August 20. It trades at $72,969, down 9.4% from the November 4 close.

BREAKING: $BTC just fell to its lowest level since August.

Over $210 million worth of longs liquidated in the past 24 hours.

The dumping continues… pic.twitter.com/R7NVGivFnD

— Crypto Rover (@cryptorover) November 12, 2026

The altcoins are doing worse. Over seven days, Ethereum has lost 16.4%, Solana 14.7% and XRP 21.3%. CoinGecko values the whole crypto market at $2.42 trillion on Thursday, and Bitcoin makes up 60.5% of it.

Leverage made every drop bigger. More than $1 billion of bets were liquidated on Monday alone, almost all of them longs, the positions that profit only if prices rise. Liquidation means the exchange closes a trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out, and those forced sales push the price down further.

So is this the flush that ends the crypto market slide, or is there more to come? The data has an answer, and it is not a comforting one.

The sell-off had no single cause. Four pieces of bad news landed one after another:

Each hit forced out more leveraged longs across the crypto market. Thursday’s slide continued the pattern on a smaller scale. We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours. Longs lost $27.6 million, against $12.3 million for shorts.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Slides Toward $73K as Nvidia Plunges 9% and MSCI Drops Saylor’s Strategy

Big liquidations usually clear out the crowd. This time, the crowd came back.

In plain terms, traders keep buying every dip with borrowed money. That leaves fuel for another round of forced selling if Bitcoin drops through the next support. Bottoms tend to come when funding turns negative and open interest falls hard, a sign that leveraged buyers have given up.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, which scores market mood from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed), reads 28 today. Fear is usually read as a buy signal. The history says it is not enough on its own.

We checked every day since February 2018 when the index sat at 28 or lower, 943 days in all, and where Bitcoin stood later.

This year’s two bottoms came with real panic. When Bitcoin hit $60,000 on February 6, the index read 9. When it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1, it read 11. Today’s 28 is fear, but it is not capitulation, the moment sellers give up all at once.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, Bitcoin has spent 2026 in a wide range. The low is $57,800 from July 1 and the high is $87,396 from late September. The midpoint is $72,598, almost exactly where Bitcoin trades now.

The price lost its 50-week exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $78,219. Its 200-week EMA sits at $69,597. Bitcoin closed below that line for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of the year’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

For the crypto market, three signs would say the bottom is close: the fear index dropping toward the teens, funding turning negative, and open interest falling as longs give up. None has shown up yet. Until they do, the 200-week EMA at $69,597 is the line that separates a pullback inside the 2026 range from a retest of the summer lows.

Morning Minute: Vitalik Recasts ETH as a Store of Value

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

🏛️ Vitalik Recasts ETH as a Store of Value

Vitalik Buterin spent Sunday on X telling Ethereum holders to stop valuing ETH as a fee-burning token and start valuing it as a store of value. “We should not feel sad if fee burn is less than 10% of breakeven indefinitely,” he wrote. “The value of ETH comes from elsewhere.”

That elsewhere is stability, which he ties to decentralization, censorship resistance and security. It replaces the ultrasound money pitch, the idea that network usage burns supply faster than staking creates it. The burn has not kept up in years. Through the first nine months of 2026 it offset about 2% of issuance while supply grew 0.64%, mostly because Ethereum’s own rollup roadmap moved activity and fees off the mainnet.

Buterin’s argument is that this is fine, and that chasing the burn would be worse. Maximizing fee revenue means wanting congestion and expensive blockspace. He warned it would turn Ethereum into “a world-scale major corporation” at the cost of what makes it worth using. The burn, he added, was “never a true floor” and came mostly from internal crypto churn like lending and “silly NFT purchases.”

Supporters are already building out the new frame. Ethlabs co-founder Binji Pande calls ETH a future-proof store of value and argues it beats Bitcoin on quantum and AI risk, citing eleven years of trading history and an Ethereum Foundation that holds under 0.2% of supply. Julian Ma of Ethlabs makes the related case that Ethereum’s security culture positions it as a programmable store of value as AI pressures cryptography.

#5206. eToro Q3 Profit Drops 74% as Crypto Trading Activity Slows

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: eToro reported third-quarter net income of about $15 million, down from $57 million a year earlier, as crypto-related activity weakened. Its funded-account base continued to grow, highlighting the difference between attracting customers and generating trading revenue from them in any particular quarter.

A trading platform can gain users even when the market becomes less profitable to trade. That tension runs through eToro’s latest financial results, which showed weaker quarterly earnings despite an expanding customer base.

According to the company’s November 10 earnings release, third-quarter net income was approximately $15 million, a decline of about 74% from $57 million in the comparable period. Net contribution came to around $186 million, down 13% year over year, with lower cryptocurrency trading activity contributing to the drop.

At the same time, eToro reported 4.39 million funded accounts, an increase of 18%, and assets under administration of approximately $20.8 billion. It also announced a $250 million share repurchase authorization.

Brokerage and trading businesses earn revenue from a mix of activity, product pricing and other services. When customers trade less frequently, a growing account base may not immediately offset the effect. The relationship is particularly visible in crypto, where transaction volumes can shift quickly as market sentiment changes.

That is why the funded-account figure and the net-contribution figure should be assessed together. One shows a measure of customer acquisition and retention; the other gives more insight into the contribution earned from services in the quarter.

Assets under administration are also distinct from eToro’s own cash and corporate assets. They reflect client-related asset values that can be affected by price movements as well as client activity.

Lower crypto activity at one trading platform does not prove digital assets are in a long-term decline. Users may trade through different venues, switch into other asset classes or simply become less active during a choppy period. The business may also earn different amounts from different types of orders.

Still, eToro’s numbers offer an operating-business perspective on the volatility seen in public-market crypto demand. NewsBTC has been tracking recent Bitcoin ETF outflows as well as uneven demand for spot Ether funds. ETF subscriptions and brokerage transaction revenues are separate metrics, but both help describe how investors are participating in the market.

A fall in net contribution can also reflect conditions in noncrypto products. Readers should avoid attributing every change in a diversified platform’s results to Bitcoin prices alone.

The $250 million repurchase authorization gives eToro permission to buy back shares under its program, subject to the company’s terms. It is not proof that the full amount was repurchased on November 10, nor does it guarantee future share-price gains.

Repurchases can alter the share count and capital allocation over time, but their effect depends on execution price, cash available and how the company balances other investments. They are best evaluated alongside earnings quality and strategic spending.

Investors should watch whether funded-account growth leads to sustained activity and improved net contribution in subsequent quarters. The product mix matters: strength in equities or other services could help offset a quieter crypto market, while increased marketing and operating costs could limit the benefit.

For crypto observers, the report is a reminder that adoption and profitability do not always move together. eToro gained funded accounts, but the softer trading environment made it harder to translate that scale into quarterly profit.

#5202. Exodus Reports $8.3M Quarterly Loss as Wallet Platform Expands Payments Business

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Exodus reported third-quarter revenue of around $32.5 million, up 7%, while swinging to an $8.3 million net loss from a profit a year earlier. The wallet company’s expansion into payments and card infrastructure adds a new commercial opportunity but also increases the importance of integration costs and execution.

Exodus built its brand around software that helps people hold and exchange digital assets without relying on a traditional centralized exchange account. Its latest results show that running a wallet business at scale now involves more than downloads and token swaps.

In its November 9 third-quarter report, Exodus said revenue reached about $32.5 million, an increase of roughly 7% year over year. The company nevertheless recorded a net loss of approximately $8.3 million, compared with a net profit of about $17 million a year earlier.

The difference between higher revenue and weaker net income points to costs and accounting items that require as much attention as transaction volume.

Exodus reported around 1.4 million monthly active users and approximately 1.4 million quarterly funded users, reflecting the scale of its consumer product. Those are company-defined measures and may overlap; they should not be added together to imply a larger distinct customer base.

The company also cited roughly $1.1 billion in quarterly swap volume. Transaction volume measures value moved through a service; it is not the same as revenue or profit. The share retained by a platform depends on fees, execution arrangements and the costs of providing the service.

This is a useful distinction across the wallet industry. A product can support heavy activity without retaining a large percentage of the value exchanged. Increased usage can even create more customer-service, compliance and technical costs.

Exodus has been extending its role in the infrastructure around digital payments. Its recent company updates describe a combination involving Baanx and Monavate and a growing emphasis on card and payment services. It has also referenced around 1.6 million active cards and substantial payment volume in the broader business context.

Payment services offer a way to make digital assets useful for routine spending rather than only investment and exchange. But building or combining regulated payment operations brings operational work: issuing relationships, settlement partners, compliance programs, fraud controls and support obligations.

NewsBTC previously covered Visa’s work on stablecoin treasury and settlement infrastructure. Exodus operates in a different part of the market, yet both stories show businesses looking for ways to make digital value move through established financial channels.

Likewise, the growing attention paid to tokenized securities infrastructure reflects a wider focus on how blockchain assets connect with ordinary financial workflows. Neither development should be mistaken for proof that Exodus’s specific payment plans will succeed.

Management cited increased general and administrative spending among the pressures on the quarter. As a company moves from a comparatively focused software product toward a broader financial-services platform, staffing, oversight and integration costs can rise before new lines generate consistent returns.

That does not make the strategy inherently flawed. It means the outcome will depend on whether additional services create more durable recurring earnings than they cost to build and operate.

The useful measures in future results will include transaction and card activity, net revenue retained from those services, the cost of operating the expanded business and whether losses narrow. Users and investors should also pay attention to security, custody arrangements and regulatory disclosures as more payment services are introduced.

Exodus is showing modest revenue growth alongside a more expensive operating model. The next several quarters will help determine whether its payments ambitions create a stronger business or simply add complexity to an already competitive wallet market.

#5201. Moody’s Taps Chainlink to Send Credit Ratings Across Multiple Blockchains

Moody’s Taps Chainlink to Send Credit Ratings Across Multiple Blockchains

Chainlink and Moody’s Ratings have completed a pilot showing how credit ratings could be beamed across multiple blockchains at once, another sign that the traditional machinery of finance is steadily moving onchain.

Announced Tuesday, the test used Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol, or CCIP, to distribute Moody’s ratings simultaneously across both permissioned and permissionless blockchain networks.

It ran through the Moody’s Ratings Token Integration Engine, or TIE, the system the 125-year-old ratings giant built to disseminate credit assessments and related data within blockchain environments. The pilot, the companies said, preserved Moody’s existing publication and governance processes while proving the ratings could travel across chains through a single interoperable layer.

The logic is straightforward: as more bonds, funds, and other assets are issued as blockchain tokens, the investors trading them will expect the credit intelligence they rely on to be available wherever those assets live, rather than stopping at any one network’s edge.

Moody’s brings real experience here, having rated or assessed more than 70 digital issuances, including digital bonds and tokenized funds, between January 2017 and October 2026.

“As more financial assets move onchain, credit intelligence has to move with them, across chains and through every rating change,” said Johann Eid, chief business officer at Chainlink Labs, calling the pilot a foundational piece of what institutional capital needs to adopt tokenization at scale.

Fabian Astic, Moody’s global head of digital economy, argued that “the future of tokenized finance is unlikely to reside on a single blockchain, platform, or market infrastructure,” and that investors will increasingly expect ratings regardless of the underlying technology.

The effort builds on Moody’s steady push onchain. Earlier this year, the firm launched TIE on the institutional Canton Network before extending it to Solana, making its ratings machine-readable on a major public blockchain.

Chainlink, meanwhile, has positioned CCIP as the connective tissue for institutional tokenization, recently rolling out an upgraded version and reporting tens of billions of dollars in cross-chain value secured as banks and asset managers experiment with moving assets between networks.

The pilot, though, ran entirely on a testnet using representative test data, with no actual rating actions published onchain and no live dissemination involved.

It demonstrated technical capability rather than a launched product, but the companies said the model is designed to accommodate future rating updates under appropriate governance. For now, it’s a proof of concept, albeit one pointing toward a future where even credit ratings are just another piece of data flowing across blockchains.

In a recent announcement, the XRPL Foundation outlined a new quantum resistance roadmap that will see the entire network upgraded to ML-DSA-44 (NIST Approved Post-Quantum Digital Signature) by 2028.

The market is becoming increasingly divided on XRP.

After invite-only early access, the desktop app from the team behind Brevis is now open to anyone on Mac and Windows.

HONG KONG, November 11, 2026: Arca, a new desktop app from the team behind Brevis, opened to the public today. Arca pays people for the AI sessions they’d otherwise throw away. It finds the session history their AI tools already keep on their computer, lets them choose which sessions to submit, strips sensitive details on the device before anything is uploaded, and pays for the sessions that are approved. Starting today, anyone can sign up with an email address, with no invite and no waitlist.

Much of today’s knowledge work runs through AI tools. People steer a model through a task, correcting it, throwing out what fails and keeping what holds up. Every one of those sessions leaves a detailed record of real work: the back-and-forth, the dead ends, the fix that finally worked. These records pile up by the thousands on people’s computers, and once the window closes, they’re worth nothing to the person who did the work. Arca gives that work a value.

Arca works with the AI tools people already use, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Claude Desktop. After installing the app, users see the sessions Arca has found on their machine, past ones included. They pick a session to upload, and Arca anonymises it on their computer before it leaves, then returns a quote range. Users either confirm, which sends the session to review, or withdraw, in which case the upload is deleted. Approved sessions are paid weekly.

Arca only reads sessions that are already on the user’s computer, and it lists everything it finds. Nothing uploads in the background, and nothing leaves the device until the user picks a session and confirms. Before a session is uploaded, Arca strips names, file paths, account details and keys, and further anonymising runs on Arca’s side.

“Every AI session is a record of real thinking and real work, and until now the person who did that work got nothing for it,” said Michael, co-founder and CEO of Brevis. “Arca lets people see what their sessions are worth and decide for themselves what to share. We opened it in small batches first to get the experience right. Today it’s open to everyone.”

Arca is built for anyone who does real work with AI, from code to contract reviews, research and long working conversations. Sessions with Claude Opus and Fable, and with the latest GPT models in Codex, qualify today, with more to come. Very short sessions don’t qualify, and every submission is reviewed before it pays. Users can connect GitHub to strengthen their profile, which can raise the value of their sessions, but it isn’t required.

Arca carries the principle behind Brevis’s verifiable computing work into a new domain: things you can verify are worth more than things you have to trust.

Arca first opened on October 13 in invite-only early access, admitting users in small batches. With today’s launch, the invite requirement is gone. Users sign up with an email address or a Google account and can start right away. Arca is free to use and available now for Mac and Windows at arca.market.

Through November 30, the Arca Launch Challenge adds $10,000 in prizes on top of regular payouts for approved sessions.

Arca pays people for the AI sessions they’d otherwise throw away. The desktop app finds the sessions people’s AI tools already keep, lets them choose what to share, anonymises sessions on the device before upload, and pays for approved sessions. Arca is built by the team behind Brevis. Learn more at arca.market.

Brevis builds verifiable computing infrastructure. Its zero-knowledge proving technology, including the open-source Pico zkVM, lets applications prove the results of complex computations. Learn more at brevis.network.

In a recent post on social media, Dogecoin engineer Michi Lumin noted that a GitHub billing issue affecting Dogecoin Core has been addressed, although uncertainty remains on how the expenses will be handled in the coming months.

Lumin disclosed that Dogecoin Core's GitHub account ran into billing issues, which she resolved by personally paying the arrears and then switching the billing to herself.

This situation follows major Dogecoin Core developer Patrick Lodder's absence on the 'core' front, with Lumin describing him as missing in action (MIA). However, Lumin clarified that this reflected her own personal experience and speculated that others might have remained in contact with him.

"So @dogecoin , Pat Lodder has gone MIA for months on the Core front (at least to ME. If others have talked to him, great!), and the Core GitHub has run into some billing issues. I've paid the arrears personally and switched billing to myself," Lumin wrote.

Responding to the offer, Lumin explained that the outstanding charges appeared to be related to GitHub Actions or continuous integration (CI) workers, whose usage is billed according to consumption.

"As far as i know, it was fees for CI workers or actions that they bill/meter.  I've been reachable but that's a whole other kettle of bees around here. Either way, it's paid right now, so we'll see how next month goes and i'll address it then if i need to," Lumin wrote.
