#5196. ARK Invest Trims Block and Bullish Positions as Bitcoin ETF Outflows Continue

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Disclosed ARK Invest trading activity points to sales of shares in crypto-linked companies Block and Bullish alongside changes elsewhere in its portfolios. A fund manager selling shares is not the same as investors redeeming money from a spot Bitcoin ETF, and the trades should not be treated as a categorical forecast for crypto prices.

Crypto markets generate several types of selling headlines, but they do not all describe the same thing. One involves investors moving money into or out of exchange-traded products. Another involves a fund manager changing which companies it owns inside a portfolio. ARK Invest’s latest trade disclosures belong to the second category.

ARK’s trade-notification service provides information about purchases and sales by its exchange-traded funds. Reporting of the November 9 trades indicates reductions in shares of Block and Bullish, both businesses tied to the wider digital-asset economy.

Trade data published for the session should be checked against the original ARK notification for exact fund allocations and amounts. Public summaries can combine activity across several ETFs, while dollar-value estimates change with the share price used for calculation.

A growth-oriented fund might sell shares to rebalance position weights, manage liquidity, fund purchases of other holdings or respond to company-specific developments. A share sale alone cannot reveal which of those motives dominated.

For that reason, it would be a mistake to describe ARK’s selling as proof that the manager has abandoned Bitcoin. The sale may reflect a view on the risk and valuation of individual equities rather than the future value of the underlying cryptocurrency.

Block’s exposure to digital assets is also different from Bullish’s. Their revenue drivers, regulation and business models are not interchangeable merely because both are routinely grouped under the label ‘crypto stock.’ Investors comparing them need to look beyond the common theme.

NewsBTC has recently tracked sizable outflows from US spot Bitcoin funds and earlier daily Bitcoin ETF withdrawals. Those figures measure net investor flows into or out of specific products, rather than an ETF manager switching between equity holdings.

Even within ETF reporting, transactions can be misunderstood. Selling shares in a listed company held by an actively managed ETF does not necessarily imply the ETF itself suffered a redemption. Likewise, a Bitcoin ETF net outflow does not automatically show why an individual investor chose to redeem.

Those distinctions become especially important in a market where the same financial firm may own Bitcoin directly, operate a fund holding mining or exchange equities, and manage entirely different technology-sector positions.

Shares of trading venues, payment companies and miners are often affected by crypto prices but can also move on earnings results, borrowing costs and capital spending. A mining company pursuing AI infrastructure may be valued on its power contracts as much as its Bitcoin output. A brokerage might add accounts while earning less from crypto transactions.

That mixture means crypto-equity portfolio changes sometimes convey a different message from spot-token trading activity. They are better read as part of ongoing active management than as standalone signals to buy or sell a coin.

The strongest verifiable facts are the securities traded, the direction of the trade and the number of shares reported for each fund. If later reporting establishes exact price-weighted values, those should be dated and described as estimates where appropriate.

ARK’s trading notices offer a window into portfolio decisions, not a complete explanation of motive. Their value for readers comes from knowing precisely what changed and avoiding the temptation to translate every share sale into a broad claim about the Bitcoin market.

#5194. Anthropic Sets IPO Price Range at $70 to $78, Valuing Company at Up to $1.4 Trillion

Anthropic Sets IPO Price Range at $70 to $78, Valuing Company at Up to $1.4 Trillion

Anthropic has set a price range of $70 to $78 per share for its initial public offering, according to an updated filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday.

The AI company plans to sell 825 million shares of Class A common stock, 801.4 million of them new shares and 23.6 million from existing shareholders, on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT," which it revealed when it made its IPO filing public last month. At the top of the range, the offering would raise about $64.4 billion, including the selling shareholders' stake. Underwriters have an option to buy a further 123.75 million shares.

Anthropic expects to price the offering on November 18 and begin trading on November 19, and is targeting a retail allocation of about 20%, well above the norm for an IPO, CNBC reported, citing people familiar with the details.

Based on the roughly 13.09 billion shares the filing says will be outstanding after the offering, the range implies a market value of about $916 billion to $1.02 trillion. On a fully diluted basis, the company could be worth up to $1.405 trillion according to CNBC, up from the $965 billion valuation it announced in a funding round in May.

Alongside the IPO, seven of the companies that supply Anthropic's computing power have agreed to buy a combined $26 billion of Class N common stock, which has no voting rights, at the IPO price. At the midpoint of the range, Google and Nvidia would each buy about $10 billion, AMD about $2.5 billion, Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft about $1 billion each, and TSMC about $500 million, according to the filing. Those shares will not be subject to the usual post-IPO lock-up period.

Anthropic expects net proceeds of about $84.6 billion from the IPO and the private placement combined at the midpoint, which it plans to use for general corporate purposes, including investment in compute and infrastructure, according to the filing.

The company reported revenue of $33.2 billion for the first nine months of 2026, up from $2.5 billion a year earlier. It posted a net loss of $104 billion over the period, most of it from a $94.3 billion non-cash charge tied to the rising value of its convertible notes and other instruments; its operating loss was $1.26 billion. Anthropic has also committed to about $900.9 billion of spending, mostly on compute and infrastructure, of which about $70.7 billion is due within the next 12 months.

Anthropic will list as a public benefit corporation with an unusual governance structure. Its Long-Term Benefit Trust, a body of financially disinterested trustees, will elect a majority of its board, while a single share of Class F stock held by an entity owned by its seven co-founders will carry 50.1% of the company's voting power on most matters, according to the filing. As a result, Anthropic will be a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules, and holders of its Class A shares will have limited influence over major decisions, the filing warns.

The range comes after a turbulent week for AI stocks. Some major investors told The Wall Street Journal last week that Anthropic's expected $1.5 trillion valuation would likely need to come down following a sell-off in AI stocks, with one suggesting a figure closer to $1 trillion. Anthropic had been eyeing a valuation of around $2 trillion as recently as September, according to an earlier draft filing.

The IPO's order book is already covered at the proposed range, CNBC reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

This article was drafted with the assistance of Claude, an AI model developed by Anthropic.

SAN FRANCISCO, November 11, 2026 — Phase, a technology company building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, today announced that Yana Prikhodchenko, former CEO of Cointelegraph, has joined the company as co-founder and CEO. She will lead strategy, global expansion and commercial development, working alongside founder Kirill Eves, as Phase scales its decentralized infrastructure for autonomous AI agents.

Prikhodchenko joins Phase after nearly five years at Cointelegraph, where she served as CEO, leading a global team of more than 200 people and transforming the company from a crypto news platform into a diversified group spanning media, marketing, research, acceleration and industry events. Before joining Cointelegraph, she spent more than a decade in senior leadership roles at major banking and insurance companies, including Allianz.

Phase is building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, giving AI agents everything they need to operate autonomously, from accessing the open web and orchestrating AI models to performing computing tasks and making payments. These services run on Phase’s Layer 1 blockchain, powered by a decentralized network of everyday devices whose owners earn rewards for validating transactions and contributing connectivity and computing power.

“AI agents are moving from answering questions to performing real tasks on our behalf, but the infrastructure they depend on was not built for autonomous systems. Phase is building an open, decentralized network that anyone can participate in. My focus is to bring this technology to developers and businesses worldwide and build the ecosystem needed to support the next generation of AI agents,” said Yana Prikhodchenko, co-founder and CEO of Phase.

“Yana brings extensive leadership experience across media, technology and financial services, along with the operational expertise and industry relationships needed to take Phase into its next stage of growth. As we bring our technology to market, she will lead the company’s commercial development and global expansion,” said Kirill Eves, founder of Phase.

Phase is a technology company building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, with four integrated services that give AI agents everything they need to operate autonomously, from accessing the open web and orchestrating AI models to performing computing tasks and making payments. The platform runs on its own Layer 1 blockchain, powered by a decentralized network of everyday devices. Phase has received $45 million in funding from its founder, Kirill Eves.

Phase Proxy enables AI agents acting on behalf of users to access websites that restrict automated traffic through mobile and residential internet connections. Phase Router intelligently directs requests across leading AI models to optimize quality, performance and cost. Phase Compute harnesses the processing power of devices across the network to run open-weight AI models, while on-chain settlement enables autonomous payments using stablecoins and PHASE, the network’s native token. Phase is building its own AI model to serve as the platform’s central intelligence, capable of advanced reasoning, solving complex tasks independently and orchestrating other AI models.

Unlike most blockchain networks that require dedicated servers or token staking, Phase allows anyone to become a validator simply by downloading the app, without specialized hardware or upfront investment. Its reputation-based consensus and randomized validator selection secure the network and prevent control from concentrating in the hands of a few powerful operators. Phase rewards device owners with PHASE tokens for validating blocks and contributing connectivity and computing power, enabling millions of people to help build the AI economy and share in the value it creates.

#5191. Bitcoin Core Breaks Silence on Three Patched Security Vulnerabilities

Bitcoin Core developers have revealed three key security vulnerabilities, including a high-severity flaw that could potentially disrupt the mining capabilities of the Bitcoin network, preventing miners from creating new blocks.

As revealed in security advisories published on Nov. 10, the vulnerabilities impacted various elements of the Bitcoin Core software that powers many nodes underpinning the world's leading cryptocurrency.

One of the vulnerabilities, titled CVE-2025-62861, was rated as a high-severity issue due to its potential effect on Bitcoin miners.

The bug has the potential to create problems after a blockchain reorganization, which is when previously accepted blocks are replaced by the network with an alternative chain.

More precisely, the issue could cause an inconsistent state in the node's mempool, where all unconfirmed transactions are stored.

The vulnerability impacted Bitcoin Core software versions 28.0-28.2 and 29.0-29.1.

It was first reported on Sept. 26, 2025, by security researcher Niklas Goegge.

Beyond the mining vulnerability, Bitcoin Core developers have announced two further security problems, rated medium severity.

The first one (CVE-2025-62859) could enable malicious network participants to slow down Bitcoin block processing through an exploit that involves changes in transaction witness data.

Under some circumstances, it could make an affected node wait for up to 10 minutes before processing a block.

Moreover, such an attack could be repeated indefinitely on the node when the latter is running in specific configurations.

The vulnerability was found by Eugene Siegel in April 2025.

The second vulnerability (CVE-2025-62860) involved Bitcoin nodes that operate on the anonymous Tor network.

In fact, the Bitcoin Core developers revealed that thousands of reachable Bitcoin mainnet nodes had been granting permissions for incoming Tor connections.

Nevertheless, the issue did not affect nodes that do not use the optional whitelist configuration.

The three vulnerabilities are not new discoveries.

In fact, all of the issues were already fixed by the Bitcoin Core developers in October 2025.

The fixes were integrated into both Bitcoin Core 30.0, which was released on Oct. 10, and Bitcoin Core 29.2, rolled out on Oct. 14.

The high-severity mining vulnerability was also patched in Bitcoin Core 28.3.

The delay in the disclosure of the vulnerabilities was in line with the Bitcoin Core security policy, which usually calls for developers to wait at least two weeks after the end of life of the last affected software version before publishing details of medium- or high-severity vulnerabilities.

The SEC has released BitMine’s Form 10-K.

According to the filing, the firm suffered a $6.3 billion net loss during the fiscal year ending August 31, 2026.

As the fiscal year runs from September 2025 to August 2026, the reported loss largely reflects Ethereum’s price decline following the October 2025 crash, which pushed ETH from a peak above $4k toward $2k.

In essence, much of the $6.3 billion loss came from unrealized losses on its ETH holdings.

The timing of the filing is also notable. BitMine has recently disclosed that it holds 6.07 million ETH, 216 BTC, and $475 million in cash and marketable securities. It also holds a stake in Beast Industries and Eightco. Altogether, its crypto, cash, securities, and moonshot investments were valued at $14.3 billion.

This demonstrates that the company has a large asset portfolio despite the large amount of paper loss they face. However, with ETH prices under pressure, continued accumulation also increases its exposure to further unrealized losses.

This brings attention to the recent thesis that Vitalik Buterin put forward regarding a new ‘store of value’ story. As previously covered by AMBCrypto, Buterin’s thesis aims to shift focus away from Ethereum’s deflationary model and instead focus on real demand for the asset.

Simply put, instead of relying mainly on reduced supply to drive value, the thesis puts greater emphasis on real demand and network adoption.

However, with BitMine alone losing $6.3 billion, it becomes an issue of whether the “demand-driven SOV” story holds when even the largest institutions holding ETH are losing significant sums.

This raises a key question: Does this put Ethereum’s long-term store-of-value narrative at risk?

For BitMine to get back into the green, Ethereum [ETH] would need a rally of nearly 50%.

However, the broader market signals suggest that recovery may not come easy. E

thereum has already underperformed Bitcoin by over 2x in Q4, falling nearly 25%. If the trend continues, the $2,000 level could come under pressure, pushing BitMine’s 6 million ETH holdings deeper into unrealized losses and adding more strain to its balance sheet.

Notably, the risk of holding such a large ETH position may also be starting to rise.

According to on-chain data, another 1,000 ETH worth $2.03 million was sold by one of the Ethereum Foundation’s wallets. Over the past week, large holders have sold a total of 17,800 ETH worth about $40 million. Meanwhile, BlackRock moved another $151 million worth of ETH to Coinbase Prime.

In essence, bulls are still not fully buying into Bitmine’s demand-driven SoV thesis.

Against this backdrop, Bitmine’s $6.3 billion in unrealized losses could put upward pressure on this scenario. As shown in the post above, BMNR is being seen by the market as a major catalyst for Ethereum becoming a SoV asset.

However, this narrative could face a reality check if ETH continues to underperform and Bitmine’s losses keep growing.

Thus, while BitMine’s 6 million ETH holdings suggest strong institutional demand, its recent SEC filing also demonstrates the dangers of such heavy accumulation, putting Ethereum’s long-term SoV story to the test.

Kraken parent Payward’s xStocks platform added tokenized versions of more than 200 stocks listed in the United Kingdom and European Union.

Token Terminal data put xStocks’ market capitalization at $1.1 billion, about 22% of the $4.9 billion in tokenized stocks the firm tracks. xStocks ranked third, behind Binance bStocks at $1.5 billion and Ondo Finance at $1.4 billion.

Payward said it plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks.

#5186. Does Holding Crypto Put Your Social Security Payments at Risk in 2026?

Home » Cryptopedia » Does Holding Crypto Put Your Social Security Payments at Risk in 2026?

Understanding SSA rules on digital assets and how ABLE accounts can legally protect your benefits.

Short answer: It depends on the type of Social Security benefits you receive.

If you receive Social Security Retirement or SSDI benefits, owning Bitcoin or other crypto generally won’t affect your monthly Social Security payments, as both of these programs don’t have asset limits.

However, if you receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI), things are different. The Social Security Administration (SSA) counts crypto as a resource. If your total countable assets exceed $2,000 for an individual, your SSI benefits could be reduced or suspended.

Note: The figures above are taken from the SSA 2026 COLA fact sheet and the SSA’s ABLE spotlight.

Much of the online confusion around cryptocurrency and Social Security stems from mixing up earned benefits with means-tested benefits:

The Social Security Administration’s (SSA) official Program Operations Manual System (POMS SI 01140.208 and SI 00830.102) outlines explicit rules for digital assets:

Consider an SSI recipient who holds $1,500 in a traditional bank account and receives $600 worth of Bitcoin as a gift:

Crypto’s market volatility introduces a unique risk for benefit compliance. If your wallet balance sits at $1,800 on October 25th, but a market surge pushes its dollar value to $2,200 on November 1st, you are technically over the SSI resource limit for November.

SSA requires beneficiaries to report changes in resources by the 10th day of the month following the change. Thus, logically, recipients must maintain accurate exchange statements, wallet screenshots, and transaction logs to verify historical values.

If you receive SSI and wish to save money without breaching resource caps, an Achieving a Better Life Experience (ABLE) account provides a legal shield:

Note: Check whether your state’s specific ABLE plan offers crypto-indexed investment options before transferring digital assets into the program.

Yes. Under the Access to Financial Institutions (AFI) program and POMS SI 01140.208 reporting procedures, SSA verifies asset balances. Recipients are legally required to disclose digital exchange accounts and self-custody wallet addresses. Failing to report crypto can lead to overpayment penalties or fraud investigations.

Cashing out converts one countable resource (crypto) into another (cash). The total dollar amount still applies to your $2,000 resource limit. However, if you sell at a profit, any capital gains can be counted as unearned income in the month realized, which could reduce or eliminate that month’s SSI check before the cash is evaluated as a resource the following month.

No. Transferring or gifting assets for less than fair market value to satisfy the $2,000 limit triggers a transfer penalty. SSA can impose a period of ineligibility for up to 36 months depending on the value of the crypto given away.

Not directly as coins. ABLE accounts only accept contributions in U.S. dollars. To move crypto into an ABLE account, you must first liquidate the cryptocurrency into cash and deposit the cash into the ABLE account (up to the $20,000 annual limit for 2026). Once inside, the funds are shielded up to $100,000 from the SSI resource test.

#5181. Solana's Jupiter Expands Beyond Trading With Token Baskets, Yield Vaults and New Portfolio

Solana's Jupiter Expands Beyond Trading With Token Baskets, Yield Vaults and New Portfolio

Jupiter, the largest trading platform on Solana, is rolling out four new products this week as it aims to expand from a place to trade tokens into an all-in-one home for onchain assets.

The company announced a new mission on Tuesday, "to make the world's assets universally accessible and useful," alongside the releases, which cover discovering, owning, earning on and managing assets.

Jupiter built its business by aggregating liquidity from across Solana so that each trade gets the best available price. It says that approach has processed more than $1.3 trillion in cumulative aggregator volume, and that its wider ecosystem now holds about $1.7 billion in total value locked, according to DeFiLlama data from early November. Its lending market has passed $1 billion in active loans, the company said.

"What Google did for information, Jupiter is doing for assets," said Kash Dhanda, Jupiter's chief operating officer. "We started with the trade because it was the hardest problem on Solana, and aggregation solved it. That taught us something: aggregation doesn't just work for trading, it works for everything."

Dhanda has framed the goal in even bigger terms. "I'm a big believer that the era of do-it-yourself DeFi is over," he said in a livestreamed interview with Incrypted on October 29, recalling having "12 tabs open and a spreadsheet" to manage positions across different venues. He said he hopes Jupiter "in five years' time will be the only money app that you need to use."

Baskets let users buy a bundle of tokens with a single SOL or USDC deposit instead of making a separate swap for each one. Baskets can follow market-cap weights or fixed targets and rebalance automatically, with every deposit, rebalance and exit routed through Jupiter for the best available price.

Jupiter Vaults is a new hub for yield strategies, from stablecoin lending to strategies backed by real-world assets, managed by independent curators rather than Jupiter itself. Users can review each strategy's risk profile, allocation and historical returns before depositing. Vaults opens on November 11 as a private beta for more than 19,000 people on its waitlist and eligible holders of staked JUP.

In the October interview, Dhanda said Jupiter's yield products are audited multiple times before reaching users. Asked what would happen if a product were exploited, he said that "especially if it's our fault, we'd like to work with users to find a good solution," and that Jupiter is exploring ways to insure such products onchain.

Portfolio V3, live now, turns Jupiter's portfolio page into a place to act on positions, with quick actions to trade, open perpetual futures, make predictions or lend, and alerts for positions near liquidation. It also adds cross-chain transfers that combine several bridges.

Pulse and rebuilt token pages are meant to make Jupiter a place to research assets as well as trade them, showing market data for tokenized stocks and ETFs, tokenomics for DeFi projects, and a sidebar for comparing tokens. Dhanda has argued that putting assets onchain is only half the job. "People talk about tokenization as if it is the end game, when in reality, it is just the first step of the game," he said in October.

The releases will roll out over the coming days, with Jupiter sharing details of each one before Solana Breakpoint, the network's annual conference, which starts on November 15.

BlackRock’s reported agreement with SBI Holdings and Startale Group concerns tokenized funds and a yen stablecoin—not a confirmed role for XRP.

Stevenson points to SBI Remit’s use of XRP for remittances and SBI’s broader XRP-related activities as reasons to watch the partnership. Her central caveat is explicit: “Nobody can tell you that this deal uses XRP.”

#5174. Bitcoin Falls as Hot US Inflation Fuels Fears of Bigger Fed Rate Hike

Bitcoin Falls as Hot US Inflation Fuels Fears of Bigger Fed Rate Hike

Bitcoin fell below $74,000 on Tuesday after U.S. inflation came in hotter than expected for the third consecutive month, adding fresh pressure to a crypto market already struggling with falling prices and investor withdrawals.

The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, above economists' forecasts of 0.3%, according to data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy prices, climbed 0.3% against expectations of 0.2%, matching September's reading for the third consecutive month.

Headline inflation actually slowed from September's 0.6% increase, but that offered little relief to traders who had expected a bigger slowdown. Both figures exceeded forecasts by 0.1 percentage points, giving the Federal Reserve another reason to keep interest rates elevated.

Bitcoin was trading near $74,200 before the announcement and briefly dropped to approximately $73,525 immediately afterward. The cryptocurrency recovered some ground toward $74,000 but remained under pressure, trading roughly 1% lower over 24 hours.

Ethereum also weakened, slipping toward $2,040 during the initial selloff, while other major altcoins faced selling pressure. Approximately $178 million in crypto long positions were liquidated within an hour of the announcement.

Liquidations happen when exchanges automatically close trades made with borrowed money because their owners no longer have enough collateral to cover potential losses. Those forced sales can push prices even lower, triggering further liquidations.

Bitcoin was already having a difficult week. The asset had lost roughly 4.5% over seven days, while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded another $201 million in net withdrawals on Monday, extending the selling pressure that preceded the inflation report.

Higher inflation usually means higher interest rates, and higher interest rates tend to be bad news for crypto. When government bonds and cash offer attractive returns, investors have less incentive to hold volatile assets such as Bitcoin, which generate no interest simply by being held.

Higher borrowing costs also reduce the availability of cheap money for speculative investments. That's why Bitcoin, despite its reputation as an inflation hedge, frequently falls when inflation data suggests the Fed will tighten monetary policy.

The latest report landed just hours after Fed Governor Christopher Waller made unusually aggressive comments about the central bank's next move.

Speaking in London, Waller said he would support a quarter-percentage-point interest rate increase in December even if inflation improved. But he also warned that another core CPI reading of 0.3% could justify a larger move.

“I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting,” he said.

October's reading hit precisely that threshold. According to Reuters, financial analysts increased their estimated probability of a 50-basis-point hike to nearly 15% by midmorning, although a smaller quarter-point increase remained the overwhelming favorite.

For context, the Fed currently holds its benchmark interest rate between 3.75% and 4%. A 50-basis-point increase would lift that range to 4.25%-4.50%, making borrowing more expensive across all of the economy.

Bond markets reacted accordingly. The two-year Treasury yield, which closely tracks expectations for Fed policy, posted its biggest increase since April 2025, while the dollar strengthened and U.S. stocks opened lower.

October's inflation report offered a mixed picture of the American economy. Food prices rose 0.5%, energy increased 0.7%, and shelter costs climbed 0.3%, accounting for more than 30% of the monthly headline increase.

Energy inflation slowed considerably from September's 5.2% surge, but price increases remained widespread across services. Recreation costs climbed 0.8%, motor vehicle insurance rose 0.7%, and medical care increased 0.3%.

The report also came with an unusual limitation: The government did not publish its standard annual inflation rate because the 2025 federal shutdown prevented the collection of October data that year. September's last available annual headline reading stood at 3.7%, well above the Fed's 2% inflation target, which is formally measured using a separate index known as Personal Consumption Expenditures.

Crypto investors have seen this pattern before. In October, Bitcoin fell after September's hotter-than-expected inflation report, and the selloff continued as rate-hike expectations strengthened.

This time, the market enters the next Fed meeting with Bitcoin substantially below its October levels and institutional demand showing signs of weakness. Higher Treasury yields could make a sustained recovery more difficult unless inflation cools or investors regain their appetite for risk.

The Fed's final policy meeting of 2026 is scheduled for December 8-9. The next CPI report will arrive on December 10, meaning policymakers will have to make their December rate decision without seeing November's consumer inflation figures.

#5171. Ripple’s Bank-Style Lending on XRPL Nears Launch: What XRP Holders Actually Get

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

The LendingProtocolV1_1 amendment on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) has collected 22 of 35 votes (62.86%).

Three more validators have signed on over the past three weeks. Ripple's own nodes have already voted yes, along with the University of Waterloo and UC Berkeley.

To go live, the amendment has to clear the 80% bar (29 votes) and hold it for two straight weeks.

The related SingleAssetVault amendment (XLS-65) has 23 votes (65.7%) and needs six more.

The XLS-65 and XLS-66 standards drop overcollateralization and instant liquidations and let companies take out fixed-term, uncollateralized loans directly on XRPL. The loans work similarly to traditional bank credit, with a fixed term and pre-set interest terms.

Ripple has already tested the protocol on a private XRPL network with nine nodes that matched the hardware of its mainnet nodes.

Holders deposit XRP or stablecoins such as RLUSD into Single Asset Vaults and receive shares. Interest is paid on a cash basis. Depositors receive it only after the borrower has sent the money. Withdrawals from a vault are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

Borrowers are vetted off-chain by Loan Brokers, who record each disbursement on the ledger. According to the XRPL documentation, the protocol "relies on off-chain underwriting and risk management to assess the creditworthiness of borrowers."

The broker's own "first-loss capital" covers losses first when a client stops paying.

Issuers can also freeze assets or claw them back. According to Ripple, all operations in a vault and in the connected lending protocol stop when an asset issuer freezes the vault.

Until now, XRP holders who wanted passive income had to use third-party bridges and wrapped tokens. After the amendment activates, holders can deposit XRP in a pool on XRPL, with its fraction-of-a-cent fees, and collect part of the interest paid by borrowers. Their income will depend on the terms set by the loan broker and on borrowers' repayments.

If a major borrower defaults and the broker's first-loss capital runs out, depositors bear the losses and their shares drop in value.

The recent Glassnode report adds another layer. As can be seen in the chart below, the largest Bitcoin liquidity cluster is concentrated around $60k. These are mostly longs opened at the bottom of the market, which haven’t been re-tested by BTC since it rallied from around $65k in August.

The key takeaway? According to Glassnode analysts, a rally to $60k could result in large amounts of long-term liquidation. However, this can create an accumulation opportunity for patient accumulators, those who are looking to take advantage of the forced selling.

The broader liquidity crunch is now weighing on the Bitcoin network.

#5169. Goldman, Citi and Global Banks Commit $270 Million to Challenge Crypto’s Stablecoin Giants

Goldman, Citi and Global Banks Commit $270 Million to Challenge Crypto’s Stablecoin Giants

The group of global banks building a joint stablecoin has put real money on the table, committing around $270 million to fund the venture as it moves from blueprint to buildout.

Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Banco Santander, and Deutsche Bank are among the institutions backing the effort, Bloomberg reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The capital is meant to cover five years of operations for a planned U.S.-incorporated company that will issue a dollar-denominated stablecoin. Known among participants as Project Faro, the venture is still searching for a chief executive, and its final name remains under discussion.

A spokesperson for the project declined to comment, as did Santander and Deutsche Bank, while Goldman and Citi referred questions to the project.

The funding is the concrete next step for an initiative that first went public late last year. As Decrypt previously reported, 21 of the world’s largest financial institutions committed in September to form a company to issue a U.S. dollar stablecoin, targeting a launch in the first half of 2027, with a euro version and other currencies to follow.

That consortium had more than doubled from an initial group of 10 banks that began exploring the idea in October 2025, and now spans North America, Europe, East Asia, the Middle East and Africa.

Beyond the four named by Bloomberg, its participants include Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Fidelity Investments, PNC, Capital One, TD Bank, UBS, BBVA, Deutsche Bank, Lloyds Banking Group and MUFG, among others. JPMorgan, notably, is not on the list.

The venture is one of several collaborative pushes by established finance into a business long dominated by crypto-native players. Visa, Mastercard and Stripe are among more than 100 companies backing the issuer Open Standard, while European banks have formed Qivalis to issue a euro-denominated coin.

At the moment, Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC together account for about 85% of a market worth roughly $290 billion, nearly all of it dollar-pegged. When the bank consortium first went public in September, Circle’s stock fell about 6% as investors priced in the prospect of bank-backed competition for USDC.

The banks are betting that institutional trust, regulatory alignment and existing client networks can win them a share of a settlement business that promises round-the-clock, cross-border payments at lower cost than traditional rails.

The token is being designed to comply with the U.S. GENIUS Act, which created the first federal framework for dollar-pegged tokens in 2025, and, where applicable, the EU’s MiCA regime. The group has said it wants the stablecoin used across wholesale, institutional and retail markets.

For now, Project Faro remains pre-launch, with no issued token, no named CEO, not even a final name, and a 2027 target that leaves ample room for delay.

But the $270 million commitment marks a shift, and a concrete signal that this bank consortium intends to compete for the onchain dollar rather than leave it to crypto.

#5165. FSB urges Turkey to tighten crypto oversight, set stablecoin rules

The Financial Stability Board cited progress on crypto licensing and urged stronger enforcement and cooperation with foreign regulators.

The Financial Stability Board (FSB) urged Turkey to tighten its oversight of crypto markets and adopt dedicated rules for stablecoins.

In a peer review published on Wednesday, the global financial watchdog said Turkish authorities had made progress by introducing registration and licensing requirements for crypto service providers.

The report was part of the FSB’s regular program of country reviews and assessed Turkey’s progress in implementing the board’s 2023 global recommendations on crypto and stablecoins. It followed a broader 2025 review that found gaps in how jurisdictions had implemented those recommendations.

The FSB recommended that Turkey begin monitoring crypto-related risks to financial stability under a formal framework, strengthen supervision and enforcement, and improve cooperation and information sharing with foreign regulators.

Turkey’s Capital Markets Board introduced licensing and operational requirements for crypto exchanges and custodians in March 2025, including minimum capital thresholds.

The FSB said Turkey had introduced safeguards including requirements to segregate assets held in custody and a ban on domestic crypto payments. The safeguards help limit the spread of crypto-related risks to banks and payment systems. Authorities also launched a centralized platform to monitor crypto activities.

The FSB’s 2025 review found that Turkey had finalized rules for crypto assets but lacked a dedicated stablecoin framework.

In June 2025, Turkey’s Finance Ministry outlined plans to introduce additional transaction checks and limits on stablecoin transfers to combat money laundering.

#5164. How to Build a Resilient Personal Investment Plan

Home » Op-ed » How to Build a Resilient Personal Investment Plan

Build a resilient personal investment plan with clear goals, diversified assets, and practical risk management. Learn how to assess costs, liquidity, and alternative investments before committing your money.

A sound investment plan ties your financial goals, time horizon, risk tolerance, and available resources together into one coherent strategy. Without that connection, even well-intentioned investment decisions can end up working against you. Diversification—spreading investments across and within asset classes rather than concentrating in a single holding—remains one of the most consistently cited principles in personal finance education. Some investors, while researching ways to diversify, come across physical assets such as gold bars as one example of exposure outside traditional stocks and bonds. This isn’t a recommendation; it’s simply an illustration of the kind of asset category investors may compare when evaluating a broader plan. This article focuses on the decision-making principles, risk management practices, and due diligence steps that apply regardless of which specific assets you ultimately choose.

Before selecting any investment, figure out what the money is actually for. Emergency savings, a short-term purchase, retirement, education funding, and long-term wealth building each come with different requirements for accessibility and acceptable volatility. Money you’ll need within the next year or two generally calls for safer, more liquid holdings. Money earmarked for goals decades away can typically absorb more fluctuation in exchange for growth potential.

It helps to separate two related but distinct concepts: risk tolerance, which is how much market fluctuation you can emotionally stomach, and risk capacity, which is your financial ability to absorb losses without jeopardizing your goals. Income stability, outstanding debt, the size of your emergency reserve, number of dependents, and investment time horizon all factor into risk capacity. Writing down your goals and constraints before researching specific investments helps prevent decisions driven by excitement or fear.

Several types of risk deserve separate attention: volatility (short-term price swings), permanent loss of capital, liquidity risk (difficulty converting an asset to cash without taking a discount), inflation risk (the erosion of purchasing power), and credit risk (a counterparty’s inability to meet its obligations).

Asset allocation refers to dividing a portfolio among categories such as stocks, bonds, cash, real estate, and alternative assets. Each category tends to respond differently to economic conditions, which is why diversification can reduce concentration risk—though it can’t eliminate the possibility of loss altogether. A realistic target allocation, one you can stick with through market stress rather than abandon at the first sign of volatility, matters more than a theoretically optimal one you can’t maintain. Rebalancing—periodically returning a portfolio to its intended mix—is a discipline rooted in preserving your chosen risk profile, not in predicting short-term market movements.

One educational approach organizes a portfolio into broad functions: liquidity for near-term needs, stability for capital preservation, growth for long-term objectives, and diversification for assets that may behave differently from your core holdings. This framework is illustrative only and shouldn’t be treated as a universal formula.

Key takeaway: A resilient portfolio begins with goals and constraints—not with chasing the latest fashionable investment.

Alternative assets are sometimes considered for diversification, potential inflation resilience, or reduced dependence on traditional financial assets. Gold, for instance, is occasionally discussed as a diversifier with no direct credit exposure, though its price can still fluctuate meaningfully. Historical behavior should never be mistaken for a guarantee of future performance.

Exposure to an asset like gold can take several forms: physical ownership, exchange-traded products, mining-company shares, or futures and other derivatives. Each form carries its own market, operational, counterparty, liquidity, and regulatory characteristics. Owning a physical asset is fundamentally different from owning a financial product whose value is merely linked to that asset’s price.

Understanding the economics of physical ownership requires a few plain-language definitions: the spot price is the current market price for immediate delivery; the purchase premium is the amount charged above spot price; the resale spread is the difference between what you pay and what you’d receive upon selling; storage and insurance costs are ongoing expenses tied to safekeeping; and liquidity describes how quickly and efficiently you can convert the asset back to cash.

Looking only at the quoted purchase price overlooks the full picture. The total cost of ownership includes premiums, storage, insurance, and eventual resale spreads. Before purchasing, it’s worth checking:

Be wary of unsolicited offers, urgency-based sales tactics, guaranteed-return claims, or requests for unusual payment methods. Compare multiple independent sources and hold on to receipts and ownership records. Product specifications, legal treatment, and tax rules vary by jurisdiction and change over time, so verify details through authoritative sources and qualified professionals.

Consider two hypothetical investors. The first spends time comparing dealers, calculates her total ownership costs, and limits her purchase to a small percentage of her portfolio in line with a written plan. The second, swayed by a high-pressure phone pitch promising rapid appreciation, commits a large sum without comparing alternatives or understanding the resale terms. The contrast says something about process quality, not about any specific asset.

Revisit your plan after major life changes—a new job, marriage, inheritance, retirement, or a significant shift in debt. Market movements alone don’t necessarily call for a strategic overhaul. Scheduled reviews should cover goal progress, emergency reserves, asset allocation, fees and ownership costs, and beneficiary or estate information. For decisions involving significant assets or complex obligations, consulting a qualified financial, tax, or legal professional is a wise move.

Before adding an alternative asset, consider:

A durable investment plan rests on clear objectives, genuine diversification, reasonable costs, adequate liquidity, and informed risk management—not on any single product. Physical precious metals may suit some financial plans, but they’re not automatically appropriate for every investor. Compare alternatives objectively, verify claims independently, and steer clear of decisions made under pressure. Take time to review your overall portfolio, write down the intended role of each holding, and seek qualified advice whenever a decision exceeds your own expertise.

This article is educational in nature and does not constitute personalized financial, tax, or legal advice. Consult a qualified professional before making investment decisions.

BitMine’s annual filing implies a nearly $2.8 billion profit for the Ethereum treasury company in the three months ended Aug. 31, driven by unrealized gains on its digital assets.

The annual accounts filed Nov. 10, compared with the nine-month statements through May, make the final-quarter result measurable for the first time.

CryptoSlate calculated the June-August figures by subtracting the cumulative nine-month amounts from the full-year totals.

BitMine reported a full-year net loss of about $6.3 billion, against a $9.1 billion loss for the first nine months. Calculations using the filings’ underlying figures imply $2.8 billion in final-quarter net income, measured before preferred distributions.

Under BitMine’s accounting policy, digital assets are measured at fair value, and changes flow through net income. A higher valuation can increase reported earnings without a corresponding cash receipt.

BitMine used $305.1 million in operating activities over the full year and $287.6 million over the first nine months. The difference is $17.5 million of operating cash used in June-August, despite the calculated profit.

#5157. Elon Musk Calls Claude Opus 5.5 a 'Masterpiece', Admits Grok 4.8 Won't Match It

Elon Musk Calls Claude Opus 5.5 a 'Masterpiece', Admits Grok 4.8 Won't Match It

Elon Musk has given a rival AI model an unusually enthusiastic endorsement while acknowledging that his own next release won't be able to beat it. Asked how Grok 4.8 would compare with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, the xAI founder answered it would be “not as good.”

“Opus 5.5 is a masterpiece,” Musk posted on X.

The admission came in a reply on X Tuesday to a question from a user named Dimdv. Musk added that Grok 5, a next generation model that will be released after this update, “should exceed Opus 5.5,” potentially in two or three months, although he gave further details for that prediction or a firm date for its release—and he’s known for not sticking to his own target dates.

For a company trying to catch up with Anthropic and OpenAI, the distinction matters. Grok 4.8 is the update Musk expects to put in some users' hands this week; Grok 5 is the model he believes could eventually put his company ahead, until competing AI companies release a new model.

The exchange began with a technical update in which Musk said Grok 4.8 had finished pretraining but was still undergoing reinforcement learning, or RL, a phase in which a model's responses are refined using feedback and rewards. He said the team had also spent considerable time cleaning up supervised fine-tuning data, the examples used to teach the model how to follow instructions.

Musk said the company had abandoned JAX, a machine-learning framework, and SGLang, software used to serve AI models, in favor of an inference and reinforcement-learning system rewritten in C and C++. Inference is the process of generating answers after a user sends a prompt; rewriting the underlying software can offer engineers more control over performance, though Musk provided no figures showing the resulting gains.

Developer tetsuo celebrated the announcement with “C wins again,” prompting Musk to clarify that the code was “C with a little C++.” He subsequently credited Starlink engineers with work that helped produce the Grok training and inference stack, pointing to SpaceX's practice of writing its own headers and handling precise time calculations, including leap seconds.

Musk described Grok 4.8 as “not yet incredible” but said its foundations were finally built correctly. He expects a soft rollout to Bot users later this week, giving the company an early test before any broader release.

Anthropic released Opus 5.5 on September 22, delivering a performance comparable to its higher-end Fable 5.1 model on most work while costing 40% less to run than the previous Opus version on typical workloads. The model targets difficult programming jobs and tasks in which AI agents work through multiple steps with limited human assistance.

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which tests whether AI agents can complete complicated tasks in a command-line environment and scores them by the percentage successfully finished, Anthropic reported 66.4% for Opus 5.5 versus 57.9% for OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra. Grok is very far behind in the leaderboards.

Musk has not published Grok 4.8 scores that would establish how large the gap really is. His immediate target is the limited rollout later this week; the promised Grok 5 challenge to Opus 5.5 is still, by his own estimate, two or three months away.

#5155. FSB pressures Turkey regulators to lock down foreign stablecoins

The FSB urged Turkey to tighten reserve checks and clarify redemption rights for foreign stablecoins on local exchanges.

The Financial Stability Board (FSB) urged Turkey to tighten safeguards for foreign-issued stablecoins sold through local crypto exchanges, calling for stronger reserve checks and clearer redemption rights in a peer review published Nov. 11.

The review points to domestic platforms as a way to oversee tokens issued abroad, and recommends targeted expectations for how those tokens maintain their peg, what backs them, and what issuers disclose.

The report itself creates no new restrictions, redemption rights, or legal obligations.

The assessment reflects information on reform progress through August 2026. Turkey has made progress on crypto-platform registration and licensing, custody separation and centralized monitoring, the FSB said.

Yet the assessment found no dedicated stablecoin issuance regime or tailored listing requirements covering stabilization mechanisms, reserve transparency, or peg history.

Existing rules cover distribution, trading and custody, alongside anti-money-laundering controls, limits on certain transfers and a prohibition on domestic crypto payments. Those controls do not fully address stablecoin-specific reserve and redemption arrangements.

report recommends that issuer rules cover effective mechanisms for maintaining stable value, prudential requirements, and clear redemption rights. For foreign-currency tokens circulating through Turkish platforms, the FSB wants targeted requirements for reserve composition and transparency, including attestations and audits.

The FSB wants Turkey to connect local platform oversight with foreign issuer safeguards. Review published Nov. 11, 2026; reform information through August 2026.

These are nonbinding recommendations. The review creates no new legal obligation or redemption right.

Qualitative map of selected safeguards, not an assessment of any token's reserves or an immediate cash-out promise.

It also calls for closer cooperation with issuers' home authorities and consideration of the regulatory and prudential rules applying overseas.

The review noted that reserve transparency, redemption practices and incident management can be difficult to assess when foreign issuers or supervisors do not provide information.

The practical issue for holders is linking a local token purchase to its backing and redemption arrangements abroad.

Stronger oversight of a Turkish distributor could improve scrutiny of those arrangements, but the FSB's recommendations do not themselves give customers a new way to cash out.

According to the review, stablecoins serve as a store of value, a hedge against lira depreciation, and a way to move liquidity between domestic and offshore platforms.

The FSB also wants Turkey to clarify how payments and e-money legislation would apply to fully backed fiat-pegged stablecoins. Its assessment said policy direction and timing had not been set, and called for safeguards separating foreign-currency stablecoins from domestic payments.

Turkish authorities viewed domestic stablecoin exposures as modest in the review. The FSB warned that wider adoption could increase currency substitution and capital-flow volatility and put pressure on bank funding.

Its recommendations call for a coordinated regulatory framework that links issuer safeguards, local distribution, and cross-border supervision.

#5154. EU Assembles Task Force To Counter Russia

Home » Regulations » EU Assembles Task Force To Counter Russia

The EU announced two initiatives to bolster the bloc’s sanctions toolbox with enhanced global presence.

The European Union’s (EU) fresh crypto-focused task force is set to tackle top sanction evading challenges, mostly ascribed to Russia. Commissioner Maria Luís Albuquerque announced this to the public following the tenth meeting of the High-Level Expert Group on Union Restrictive Measures.

After the gathering in Brussels, this new EU regulatory arm aims to close gaps that allow Russia to sustain economic activity amid ongoing sanctions linked to its Ukraine invasion. The meeting brought together senior representatives from EU countries, the European Commission, and the External Action Service.

INTEL: EU sets up crypto task force to stop Russia dodging sanctions with digital assets

The examination of emerging financial threats revolves around crypto currency as a safe haven for tax or sanction evasion, keeping a strong commitment to Ukraine. Complementing the task force represents a broader dedicated sanctions office within the EU Commission. This improves coordination across member states.

The G7 is taking a more unified stance across policy, outreach & implementantion. It builds on 21 successive EU sanctions packages on Russia that have gradually targeted crypto-powered channels. Over the next 12 months, intelligence sharing and support from Ukraine and the UK will be used  to identify regular circumvention methods.

The latest sanction package, penned last Summer, freshly imposed transaction bans on 14 third country crypto platforms, enabling potential full bans on crypto services as well. By focusing on detection, enforcement consistency & international cooperation, the EU seeks to limit Russia’s ability to maintain economic resilience, still prevalent even after a flurry of sanction packages.

EU Launches Crypto Task Force to Crack Down on RussiaThe European Union has established a dedicated Crypto Sanctions Task Force to tackle sanctions evasion through digital assets.Announced on November 6, the program seeks to address the means through which Russia can evade… pic.twitter.com/uYJkWjr0Ez

Meanwhile, Russia recently implemented a new digital-asset focused law, lifting transaction & investment bans for retail customers that pass a special knowledgeability test. For businesses, the landscape has shifted too: Russian currency exchanges are able to legally offer crypto services from November 22, 2026, abiding by the legal framework from the local bank authority.

With the geopolitical situation evolving, cross-border transactions powered by the blockchain is seen as a seamless way to lift sanctions & off-day barriers, but it also facilitates a gray area of liquidity for military-industrial circumvention, off-record energy exports & often shadow fleet operations. To mitigate the risks, the EU’s new task force launched new enforcement measures.

#5152. Near AI Breach Exposes User Details and Data From 18 AI Agents

Near AI Breach Exposes User Details and Data From 18 AI Agents

Near AI has disclosed a breach that exposed account information belonging to about 100 users and data from 18 AI agents after an attacker exploited software running its servers.

The company said in a November 9 report that an attacker used a remote code execution vulnerability in SGLang, an open-source engine that runs AI models and generates responses to user requests.

The exploit allowed the intruder to execute commands on one inference server and then reach other parts of Near AI’s infrastructure.

Investigators traced the intrusion to an internal system connected to Private Chat, a feature the company had already retired. The attacker downloaded names and email addresses for approximately 100 users, along with subscription plan and account balance information for some of them.

Another 18 agents were accessed on an older deployment of Near AI Agents, where the attacker retrieved their chat histories, settings and logs. Those agents were not running inside NEAR AI’s confidential computing environment, which is designed to shield information from the company operating the servers.

Logs also exposed NEAR AI Cloud API keys belonging to two customers. These keys function like digital credentials that applications use to access cloud services; Near AI says it has revoked both, but did not say whether the attacker used them.

Near AI found no indication that stored Private Chat conversations or uploaded files had been accessed. The confirmed theft involved account records and legacy agent data, while exposure of live confidential requests remains a possibility identified by the investigation.

Hardware isolation does not guarantee that the software inside the protected environment is safe. “It does not protect against a vulnerability in the software running inside the environment,” Near AI acknowledged, explaining that the SGLang flaw let the attacker run code where confidential requests were being processed.

SGLang had already attracted scrutiny from security researchers. In July, Carnegie Mellon University’s CERT Coordination Center documented six vulnerabilities in the project, including bugs that could let attackers execute commands or expose credentials, depending on how servers were configured.

Near AI did not identify the specific SGLang flaw exploited in this incident, so there is no basis to link the breach to any of those earlier disclosures. It reported the vulnerability to SGLang’s developers.

Near, to its credit, was quick to fix the issues.

“On detection, we revoked all active sessions and administrative credentials, replaced all agent tokens, took Private Chat offline, and deployed a fix for the SGLang vulnerability across all inference servers,” the project said.

”We've completed the rotation of all remaining credentials and a full forensic review. We have notified users whose account details or agents we have confirmed were accessed and will make any regulatory notifications that are required.”

Near AI notified users whose account records or agents it confirmed were accessed and says it will make any required regulatory notifications. It also warned users to be wary of unsolicited messages referring to their Near AI accounts or balances, and contacted the owners of all 18 affected agents individually.

The public summary leaves merchant counts, geography, payment-value concentration and conversion treatment unspecified. Those gaps limit any attempt to extend the findings to global merchant market share or determine whether a few large customers dominate the result.

The practical test for merchants is whether the routes they offer match their customers’ incoming payments at an acceptable full cost. Broader, comparable merchant coverage would be needed to turn one processor’s experience into a global assessment of Base.

#5149. Xash Brings Gold Rewards to Solana Stablecoin Users

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » Xash Brings Gold Rewards to Solana Stablecoin Users

The platform aims to tackle DeFi’s reliance on short-term incentives.

Xash, a Solana-based application that rewards users with tokenized gold for stablecoin activity, has announced its public launch at Solana Breakpoint 2026 in London, scheduled for November 15–17.

The platform aims to change how users earn rewards in decentralized finance (DeFi) by offering gold instead of temporary token incentives. Users can earn rewards by lending stablecoins, providing liquidity and trading across established Solana DeFi platforms.

The launch comes as DeFi protocols continue to face a challenge: attracting users who stay after promotional rewards expire. Xash is betting that gold-backed rewards could offer a more sustainable alternative.

Many DeFi platforms use token rewards to attract deposits and trading activity. However, users often move their funds elsewhere once those incentives end, creating a cycle known as mercenary capital.

Xash wants to address this problem by rewarding ongoing stablecoin activity with tokenized gold rather than short-lived token campaigns.

The company says the approach is intended to encourage longer-term participation in DeFi while giving users an opportunity to accumulate gold.

It also aims to benefit DeFi platforms seeking sustained activity and stablecoin issuers looking to expand the use of their tokens.

“Stablecoins don’t have a supply problem. They have a usage problem. Incentive campaigns rent users for a few weeks, then they’re gone,” said Kevin Huynh, co-founder and CEO of Xash.

Xash aggregates DeFi opportunities into a single interface, evaluating available strategies daily and presenting users with options based on potential gold rewards.

Before committing funds, users can review associated costs and estimated 30-day rewards. They can then select an opportunity and authorize transactions directly through their own wallets.

As part of the launch, the company is introducing direct withdrawals of accumulated tokenized gold rewards to users’ wallets. It is also adding a curated liquidity vault built on Kamino, allowing users to deploy stablecoins through a single deposit instead of managing individual transactions.

Xash says its trading activity does not involve directional price bets or borrowed funds. However, this does not eliminate the risks associated with DeFi. Users remain exposed to the underlying protocols and market conditions, including potential losses when using the Kamino vault.

The project was founded by Kevin Huynh, who serves as CEO, alongside Vinny Lingham, co-founder of Civic and Gyft and a former general partner at Multicoin Capital; Alen Ribic, co-founder of SweepSouth; and Llew Claasen, former executive director of the Bitcoin Foundation.

Xash’s launch comes amid growing demand for tokenized real-world assets (RWAs), particularly gold-backed digital tokens.

According to the World Gold Council, the tokenized gold market has expanded fivefold since late 2024, reaching approximately $6 billion.

Trading activity has also accelerated. Tokenized gold generated more than $90 billion in spot trading volume during the first quarter of 2026 alone, surpassing the total recorded throughout 2025, according to CoinGecko research.

Xash tests whether real-asset rewards can retain DeFi users better than short-term token incentives. Its launch also reflects rising demand for tokenized gold within the Solana ecosystem.

#5148. Bitcoin Covenants Part 5: MATT and OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY — How Bitcoin could carry state across transactions

OP_CCV embeds contract state directly into Taproot output keys and enforces valid state transitions onchain. This makes it possible to achieve stateful contracts and compact fraud proofs.

This is Part 5 in the technical article series about Bitcoin covenants by Cointelegraph Research. To read the previous article click here.

MATT (Merkleize All The Things) is a smart contract framework for Bitcoin that enables stateful contracts and scalable fraud proofs. A stateful contract carries information forward across multiple transactions and can update this information as the contract evolves. Standard Bitcoin scripts do not provide this capability, because each transaction is evaluated independently with no memory of previous executions.

Every covenant proposal allows state-carrying UTXOs to an extent, as illustrated by scripting languages such as Sapio, which builds on OP_CTV. This works by using addresses to represent a finite state automaton, where transactions function as the state transitions. However, there is no way to elegantly implement numerical logic in this paradigm, a gap filled by MATT, and in particular its proposed implementation through OP_CCV. Because MATT allows committed data to be computed at spend time and re-embedded into the next output, each spend can derive a new state dynamically, instead of choosing from a predetermined set of states.

To understand the MATT proposal, it is useful to first review how Taproot commits data through public keys. Every Taproot output contains a base public key, called the internal key, which can be cryptographically modified or “tweaked” to commit to extra information. Formally, the tweaked public key is Q = P + t·G, where P is the internal key, G is the generator of the secp256k1 elliptic curve, and t is a tagged hash of P and the committed data.

In a regular Taproot output, this commitment typically encodes the Merkle root of a taptree, which contains hidden spending paths. MATT builds on this mechanism to also embed contract state into the key. Instead of embedding complex logic directly in Bitcoin’s scripting language, MATT encodes computation as a sequence of state commitments, and the chain verifies only that each state transition is valid.

MATT can be realized through different opcode combinations. The most direct and well-specified implementation relies on OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY (OP_CCV). OP_CCV provides the primitive that makes state-carrying UTXOs feasible within Taproot.  OP_CCV allows a script to verify that a Taproot input or output key has been tweaked to commit to a specific piece of state data. The internal key is first tweaked with a hash of the contract’s current state, and then Taproot’s standard taptree tweak is applied on top. The resulting output key therefore commits to both the tapscript  (the set of spending conditions) and the current state of the contract.

OP_CCV can then enforce what state is carried forward into the next output. It allows the script to inspect the state data provided on the witness stack, perform computations on it, and require that the resulting updated state is correctly re-committed in a specified output. This is how state transitions are enforced on-chain. The stack format is:

OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY

The opcode supports three modes for checking an output as well as a separate input mode. In default mode, the entire BTC value of the input UTXO is allocated to the specified output; in deduct mode, only a portion equal to the output’s amount is assigned, leaving the remainder available for further outputs; and in ignore mode, the script and data commitment are verified without constraining the amount.  Because default and deduct modes are designed to preserve value across checked outputs, transaction fees must be paid through separate fee-paying inputs. A dedicated fee input and change output can be added to the transaction without conflicting with the covenant’s constraints. This prevents the accidental burning of funds that can occur in more primitive covenant implementations, such as OP_CTV or SIGHASH_ANYPREVOUT. It also addresses a major limitation of presigned-transaction-style covenants, which typically define amounts upfront and therefore cannot accommodate dynamic fee adjustments or partial unvaults.

When OP_CCV is combined with OP_CAT, the full MATT framework becomes even more expressive. OP_CAT enables byte concatenation in Script, which makes it possible to construct and verify Merkle proofs directly on-chain. Two distinct Merkle trees are associated with a Taproot output in such an arrangement. The first is the familiar Taproot script tree (the taptree), whose leaves are the contract’s spending scripts. The second is a separate state tree, whose leaves are the contract’s data, such as the intermediate steps of a computation.  The OP_CCV + OP_CAT script can verify a Merkle proof against the current state tree root, compute the updated root after a transition, and use OP_CCV to force the next output to commit to it.

This construction enables fraud-proof systems with a slashing condition in which a long computation is committed off-chain, and only the specific disputed step (with its path in the binary tree) needs to be revealed and verified on-chain. Similar systems exist as optimistic rollups on other blockchain systems: the full computation runs off-chain, and the on-chain contract only intervenes when someone raises a challenge. Fraud proofs require that the computation be compiled down to a binary circuit or equivalent step-by-step representation that can be committed to in a Merkle tree. OP_CCV + OP_CAT would avoid the need for the Lamport one-time signatures and pre-signed transaction graphs that BitVM relies on to enforce state consistency.

Beyond fraud proofs, the OP_CCV and OP_CAT combination also has implications for vaults. OP_CCV alone can implement vaults, but when combined with OP_CAT, it allows fully featured vaults that are essentially equivalent to the functionality proposed by OP_VAULT. As James O’Beirne, the author of OP_VAULT, has noted, OP_CCV represents a more general and robust design that effectively supersedes his earlier proposal.

In the next article in this series, we will move on from general covenant proposals to review application-specific opcodes such as OP_VAULT, OP_UNVAULT, and OP_EVICT. Each of the opcodes are designed to solve a specific problem rather than provide broad programmability.

#5147. Nvidia Erases 2026 Gains as Republicans Threaten Jensen Huang With Subpoena

Nvidia Erases 2026 Gains as Republicans Threaten Jensen Huang With Subpoena

Nvidia shares plunged to $166.95 Tuesday afternoon, leaving the AI chipmaker down 18.42% for November and wiping out all the gains it had accumulated in 2026.

The selloff accelerated as congressional Republicans threatened to subpoena CEO Jensen Huang over his reported relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.

At that price, Nvidia was roughly 10.5% below its $186.50 closing price at the end of 2025 and 31.4% below its recent $243.37 peak. November is shaping up as its worst month since September 2022, when shares lost roughly 19.6%; the company suffered an even deeper 32% crash in April of that year.

Tuesday's drop exceeded 6% in afternoon trading, after a 4.3% fall on Monday. The two-day decline was on track to erase more than $470 billion in market value. Even after the significant drop, some analysts would still view the stock as extremely overbought in the long term, with prices much higher than what would be considered safe based on technical indicators.

Just for context, even an additional 20% crash (-43% from October) would be considered healthy in an isolated technical analysis, leaving the price still above the average price of the last 50 months. Prices tend to either bounce or trade near that line. When prices go too far away from the average, that usually means there is an unusual appetite for the asset, typically driven more by FOMO than fundamentals.

House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast told ABC News on Tuesday that he was prepared to subpoena Huang unless the CEO responded by Wednesday, November 11, to a request for a closed-door briefing. No subpoena had been issued at the time of the report.

Mast and two other Republican committee chairs asked Huang to appear on November 18 and explain his interactions with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip buyer Megaspeed. The lawmakers also want details about Nvidia's safeguards against foreign espionage, according to a letter reviewed by Reuters.

U.S. authorities have reportedly investigated whether Alice Huang, who has no family relationship to the Nvidia CEO, passed information to Beijing. The allegations have not established that Jensen Huang knowingly disclosed confidential information or violated export rules.

On Sunday, Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into whether its chief executive was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The board said it had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets were compromised, but would examine the available information.

Earlier today, the Financial Times reported Nvidia has hired former U.S. prosecutor Joon H Kim to conduct the internal investigation.

The company is also facing legal pressure. Shareholders filed a proposed class-action lawsuit Monday alleging that Nvidia and Huang failed to disclose risks associated with the reported relationship.

The scandal has landed during a broader reassessment of the AI boom. Investors have questioned how long massive spending on data centers can continue, and Nvidia's competitors are offering customers more alternatives to its expensive chips.

Google introduced new AI chip configurations Monday. The Information reported that OpenAI was considering buying Google's tensor processing units, or TPUs, which are processors built specifically to run AI workloads. Neither company has confirmed a purchase but yesterday Google announced a new line of TPUs available for select customers, directly competing against Nvidia’s chips.

Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly earnings on November 17, one day before the congressional briefing requested by House Republicans. Mast's deadline for Huang to respond comes first, on November 11.

#5146. Finland Turns Bitcoin Miners Into Discounted Home-Heating

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Finland Turns Bitcoin Miners Into Discounted Home-Heating

In the town of Nokia, Finland, a 180-square-meter house now relies entirely on Bitcoin mining rigs for warmth.

During the frigid months of winter in Northern Europe, heating efficiency is the main topic of discussion even in the richest neighborhoods. The frequently hostile surroundings have urged heating specialists to come up with new, creative ways to replace traditional oil heating with cutting-edge technology.

That’s where Bitcoin (BTC) comes into play: Finnish homes have already adapted liquid-cooled mining machine heaters. They utilize the gains equipped from Bitcoin (BTC) mining venues to offset the costs of heating. On the other hand, that kind of solution is highly-dependent on the hash-rate difficulty across the network, among factors like general market conditions.

The next BTC block-reward halving comes in 2028, which could arguably cap the profits of this kind of business if Bitcoin (BTC) crosses $135,000. With installation costs exceeding $20,000, SunBit’s Bitcoin Boiler is aimed at relieving high-heating costs for the residents of Finland. The machine is supposed to work in-profit as long as Bitcoin’s price stays above $70,000.

Some people use Bitcoin mining to make money.In Finland, people are using it to heat their homes.A Finnish startup called SunBit has installed Bitcoin mining machines that double as home heating systems.The concept is pretty wild.Instead of letting the heat generated by… pic.twitter.com/9S4hqTYSl6

For instance, in a historical house in Tampere, Finland’s third-largest city, mining rigs replaced wood burning, maintaining a 1,500-liter water tank between 50°C and 60°C. Sunbit’s liquid-cooled Bitcoin miner utilizes the Antminer S21 XP Hydro, employing a hash rate of up to 495T. The device consumes 5.3 kilowatts of power & draws about 46,400 kWh annually.

The Bitcoin Boiler device stores this heat in water, reaching temperatures up to 60 degrees Celsius, which is then circulated throughout the house via radiators and underfloor heating pipes. It costs roughly $5,200 a year to run. SunBit founder Elmeri Suomi stated: “The heating function itself is unaffected by market conditions; only the payback period changes.”

🇫🇮 🔥 Underground Bitcoin mining in Finland is used to heat its towns, instead of being wasted. pic.twitter.com/EHOfxcWq6M

Bitcoin-based heating systems have first been tested in the Netherlands, but Finland’s adoption mark has grown way further. The Bitcoin Boiler service fee is optional and includes 24/7 remote monitoring with automatic heating strategy optimization aligned with Finland’s floating electricity prices. This runs in a companion app with grid peak-shaving options for advanced enthusiasts.
